41be12447155aef4: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesian police said Malaysian authorities have arrested the owner of the MT Global 168 tanker, which was intercepted with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine on board.
Indonesian National Police (Polri) Narcotics Crime Director Brigadier General Kristian Parluhutan Siagian said Malaysian police had informed them of the arrest.
He said Malaysian authorities had earlier sought information related to the investigation, including telephone numbers, the identities of suspects and their links to the ketamine smuggling network.

"This afternoon, we received information from the Malaysian police that they had also arrested the ship's owner," he was quoted as saying by Indonesian news portal Kompas.com at a press conference at the police headquarters in South Jakarta yesterday.
Kristian said Malaysian authorities had found indications that the vessel had repeatedly changed names, allegedly to conceal its identity and involvement in illegal activities.
"Regarding ownership, they have informed us that the vessel keeps changing its name, which indicates that it is being used for illegal activities," he said.
However, he said Polri had yet to receive the identity of the arrested owner.
"We do not have the name or initials yet; they are the ones who made the arrest," he added.
The case came to light after authorities intercepted the tanker on Oct 20 in waters off Tanjung Balai Asahan, North Sumatra.
A search of the vessel uncovered 58 sacks containing 1,160kg of ketamine. Laboratory tests confirmed that the seized substance was ketamine hydrochloride (HCl).
Polri later identified a Taiwanese national, known only as YCY, as a suspect in the case.
He is believed to have acted as the vessel's manager and controlled the ketamine consignment.
Meanwhile, seven Indonesians initially detained in connection with the case have been released after investigations found that they were unaware of the drugs on board.
The seven were replacement crew members who claimed they had been hired to transport oil.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Hussein Omar Khan for comment.
552215ba947837b8: KUALA LUMPUR: Job fulfilment plays a bigger role than salary in determining whether Malaysian employees intend to stay with their employers, with 91 per cent of highly fulfilled workers planning to remain at their workplace compared with just six per cent of those who feel very unfulfilled.
The findings are from the Singapore and Malaysia Salary Guide Report 2027 by Omni HR, an Asia-Pacific human resources and payroll platform, in partnership with PAYGAP Asia.
The report found that while competitive pay contributes to employee retention, job fulfilment has a considerably stronger influence on workers' intention to stay.

The proportion of employees planning to remain with their employers rises from 47 per cent among those earning at least 20 per cent below their peers to 63 per cent among those earning at least 20 per cent above them.
However, the gap is significantly wider when measured against job fulfilment.

The report found that 75 per cent of highly fulfilled employees earning at or below their peers' salaries planned to stay, compared with only 25 per cent of unfulfilled employees earning above their peers.

It also highlighted the importance of career progression, with Malaysian employees seeing a median promotion-related salary increase of 14 per cent, 2.8 times the five per cent median increase for routine pay adjustments.
The report noted that salary progression between entry-level and senior positions was also steeper in Malaysia than in some other regional markets.
"An engineering director earns about six times the pay of an entry-level engineer, compared with about three times in Singapore for instance.
"In finance, a director earns about four times the pay of an associate in Malaysia and about 2.6 times in Singapore," the report detailed.
Meanwhile, 26 per cent of Malaysian employees had gone at least 12 months without a pay adjustment, rising to 36 per cent among those with more than a year of tenure.
Employees who had not received a pay change in at least a year were 2.5 times more likely to resign, according to the report.

Omni HR chief executive officer Brian Ip said while salary was often the first factor employees compared, whether they found their work rewarding and considered pay increases fair also carried significant weight in their decision to stay.

"Pay is the first thing employees compare, because it is easy to measure. Whether the work feels rewarding and whether a raise feels fair are harder to see, and the evidence shows they carry more weight in whether people plan to stay," he said.
The report recommended that employers incorporate job fulfilment into regular employee check-ins, alongside reviewing salary competitiveness and career progression.
It also suggested that employers track employees who had not received pay adjustments in the preceding 12 months to identify potential retention risks.

The report combines anonymised payroll and human resources records from more than 200 employers on Omni HR's platform across seven Asia-Pacific markets, alongside salary and employee sentiment submissions from professionals on PAYGAP Asia.

2f6c73dff3c31a9e: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) wants the Health Ministry to conduct an immediate nationwide audit of critical hospital infrastructure following a reported power failure during surgery at a Sabah hospital.
Its president, Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan, said the incident, if confirmed, was unacceptable and raised serious concerns over patient safety and the reliability of essential hospital systems.

"No patient should have to undergo surgery under such conditions, while doctors should not be forced to compromise patient care because of failures in essential hospital systems," he said in a statement today.
He said reports of recurring air-conditioning breakdowns, electricity and water supply disruptions, and failures of backup power systems were particularly alarming.
"These are not minor maintenance issues. They can directly affect patient safety, infection control and the delivery of timely medical care," he said.
Dr Sivanaesan said the ministry should investigate the reports and conduct an urgent nationwide audit, particularly of operating theatres, intensive care units and delivery rooms.
Hospitals experiencing such failures should be prioritised for immediate remedial action, he added.
"Patient safety cannot depend on the resourcefulness of doctors working around failing infrastructure," he said.
He said healthcare professionals must be provided with safe and reliable facilities to deliver the standard of care expected by Malaysians.

A doctor at a Sabah hospital was previously reported to have used a mobile phone flashlight to stitch up a patient after a power outage interrupted a routine operation in the obstetrics and gynaecology department.
Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) told the Dewan Rakyat on Nov 17 that the incident was compounded by the absence of a functioning uninterruptible power supply (UPS).
He also highlighted recurring breakdowns of the hospital's operating theatre air-conditioning system and disruptions to electricity and water supply, which had affected operations.

622b1398bfbb6aeb: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation edged up to 1.9 per cent in October from 1.8 per cent in September, driven mainly by higher transport costs and electricity, gas and fuel prices.
The Statistics Department said the transport group recorded the sharpest increase, with inflation rising to 4.2 per cent from 2.5 per cent the previous month.
The increase was largely driven by the cost of operating personal transport, which rose 4.9 per cent compared with 2.7 per cent in September.
The department said the average market price of RON97 petrol increased to RM5.00 per litre in October from RM4.64 in September, while diesel rose to RM5.20 per litre from RM5.05.
The average market price of RON95 petrol also increased to RM4.52 per litre from RM4.16, compared with the subsidised price of RM1.99 per litre.
Inflation in the housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels group also accelerated to 1.9 per cent from 1.4 per cent, following a sharp increase in electricity, gas and fuel costs.
The subgroup recorded inflation of 4.7 per cent in October compared with just 0.1 per cent in September.
The department partly attributed the increase to the revision of the Automatic Fuel Adjustment rate for domestic electricity users in Peninsular Malaysia consuming more than 800 kilowatt hours (kWh).

Meanwhile, the food and beverages group, which carries the largest weight in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 29.8 per cent, recorded slower inflation of 1.7 per cent compared with 1.8 per cent in September.
Food prices at home remained unchanged at 1.2 per cent, while inflation for food consumed outside the home eased to 2.5 per cent from 2.6 per cent.
Other groups recording higher inflation included alcoholic beverages and tobacco, at 2.9 per cent, and furnishings and household equipment, at 0.5 per cent.
However, inflation in restaurant and accommodation services eased to 2.1 per cent from 2.2 per cent, while education moderated to 1.8 per cent from 2.1 per cent.
Personal care and miscellaneous goods and services recorded a sharper moderation, falling to 1.2 per cent from 2.8 per cent.
On a state level, seven states recorded inflation above the national rate of 1.9 per cent.

Negri Sembilan recorded the highest rate at 2.6 per cent, followed by Kedah at 2.5 per cent, Johor and Putrajaya at 2.3 per cent each, Pahang and Labuan at 2.2 per cent each, and Selangor at 2.1 per cent.
On a month-on-month basis, inflation rose 0.1 per cent in October, unchanged from September.
The CPI increased to 137.7 points in October from 135.1 points in the corresponding month last year.

02c572bd77a67b44: KUALA LUMPUR: Cable theft disrupted the signalling system along the Bukit Mertajam railway line today, causing delays of up to 80 minutes to Electric Train Service (ETS) and KTM Northern Sector services.
Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB), in a Facebook post, said the disruption was expected to cause delays of more than 60 minutes from the original train schedules.

Several ETS and KTM Komuter Utara services continued to experience delays.

d53249b6120fc862: BENTONG: A motorcyclist was rescued after clinging to an oil palm tree for safety when fast-moving floodwaters swept him off a flooded stretch of Jalan Telemong-Chemomoi near Karak yesterday.

The man, believed to be in his 40s, had been travelling alone from Chemomoi towards Telemong when he attempted to cross the inundated road and was swept into an oil palm plantation along with his motorcycle. Passers-by pulled him to safety using a steel cable at 8pm.
Pelangai assemblyman Datuk Amizar Abu Adam posted a one-minute-and-10-second video of the rescue on his Facebook page.

The footage showed two men wading through chest-deep floodwaters to reach the victim before throwing him a steel cable attached to a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle parked nearby, as torrents of water rushed around him.
"It was a tense moment as the owners of several 4WD vehicles crossing the flooded stretch used a steel cable to reach the victim and pull him to safety before he was swept away further.
"The victim was eventually rescued," Amizar said in the caption accompanying the video.
Meanwhile, heavy rain yesterday caused flash floods in several low-lying residential areas and business premises in Karak town.
Several roads, including those in Taman Permai, Karak Avenue and Jalan Chemomoi in Pelangai, were inundated and impassable to light vehicles.
Videos and photographs of floodwaters surging across roads and inundating business premises circulated widely on social media, though the water has since receded in most affected areas.

baa52bf78e608a2a: SHENZHEN: US president Donald Trump hailed his great “friendship” with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and downplayed a spying scandal involving Nvidia, just hours before leaders of the world’s top two economies meet for talks in China.

“I was with president Xi all night last night, sitting next to him at the dinner, right on his right hand side, and we spoke the whole evening,” Trump told Fox News on Thursday on the sidelines of this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern city of Shenzhen.

When asked if the downfall of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, a prominent opponent of restrictions on chip sales to China, came up in conversation with Xi at a banquet on Wednesday evening, Trump said: “I might have referred to it just briefly because it’s such a tragedy.”

Trump is slated to hold his third summit of the year with Xi later on Thursday, with the fallout from the Nvidia scandal threatening to upend a fragile trade truce set to expire on Jan 10. Washington unleashed new chip curbs earlier this week designed to thwart Beijing’s ability to train frontier AI models, prompting Beijing to warn of countermeasures if the two sides can’t reach a resolution.

Despite the underlying tensions, Xi personally greeted Trump upon the US president’s arrival at the airport on Wednesday, returning a favour for Trump’s in-person welcome when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September. The unusual gesture marked the first time in roughly 50 years that a Chinese leader met a visiting dignitary on the tarmac.

Trump lauded that welcome and sought to downplay reports that Huang had conducted an affair with a Chinese executive that US intelligence believes was spying for China. “Any pretty woman that comes from China, they considered her to be a spy,” he told Fox. “She was a businesswoman who bought chips.”
Beyond the airport pageantry, expectations are low for major breakthroughs given both leaders are meeting again at the Group of 20 leaders’ summit in Miami next month.

The two sides are looking to advance tariff reductions on US$30 billion worth of each other’s imports, negotiated under the newly established US-China Board of Trade. A similar framework has been floated for bilateral investment, though progress has been slow.

Xi urged Apec members to reduce barriers to trade and investment in his opening remarks at the leaders’ meeting on Thursday morning, calling for an “open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation.”

Trump and Xi are also expected to meet with Russian leader Vladimir Putin this afternoon in what would be an unprecedented summit between the three men, who together control at least 90% of the world’s nuclear weapons.

Trump and Xi last year reached a truce to end their trade war, and agreed to extend it to early next year during their September meeting in Washington. Under that deal, in which both sides agreed to tariff reductions, an understanding was reached for the Trump administration to hold off imposing new tech curbs against Beijing in exchange for a steady flow of critical minerals from China.

That bargain has increasingly come under strain. US officials have repeatedly complained that America isn’t getting rare earths at the expected volume and pace - a grievance treasury secretary Scott Bessent and US trade representative Jamieson Greer raised with Chinese vice premier He Lifeng in a video call earlier this month.

The US commerce department this week published interim rules that would restrict China’s remote access to high-end AI chips hosted in overseas data centres. If thoroughly enforced, the regulation could deal a heavy blow to China’s AI ecosystem by shutting off a crucial source of computing power for Chinese developers racing to build cutting-edge models. The move drew a sharp rebuke from China’s commerce ministry.
The Xi-Trump meetings this year have been more about atmospherics and keeping the broad relationship stable than substantive negotiations on trade, investment and security matters.

Asked how the American people can tell if Thursday’s meeting is a success, Trump told Fox News: “I think I’ve already gotten that headline, because the relationship that I have with China is a great one.”

“The fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people, the young children, the soldiers, the whole thing — it was a great respect, and I appreciate that,” Trump said. “That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China, too.”

600d5232d489768b: WASHINGTON: A federal judge said on Wednesday the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency "made a mockery of court orders" in Colorado and that the court found government officials in contempt for instantly re-arresting a man whom the judge had ordered released.
US District judge Charlotte Sweeney declined to take any further action because she said the officials had "cured the contempt by ceasing the practice at issue" as sworn by an official in court.

"ICE's new 'policy' of immediately re-detaining petitioners following release made a mockery of court orders mandating petitioners' immediate release," the judge wrote, according to court records in the US District Court for the District of Colorado.

At least 18 people in Colorado have been held in detention longer than they should have been or have been re-arrested within minutes of their judge-ordered release in the past six weeks, CPR News, the news division of Colorado Public Radio, reported.
The report said that immigration attorneys estimated the number may be higher given that some immigrants represented themselves.

ICE, which ​is part of ​the department of homeland security, has been ⁠the face of Republican president Donald Trump's immigration crackdown and deportation drive that rights groups say has violated free ​speech and due process rights.
Human rights groups also say ​the ⁠crackdown has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

The Trump administration has maintained that its actions aim to improve domestic security and are in compliance with the law. ICE and DHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment on what the judge said on Wednesday.
⁠Democrats, ​who won majorities in both chambers of ​Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, say they aim to hold the Trump administration accountable for ​its immigration policies.

eed403a286b1a0fd: PETALING JAYA: Umno is set to lose its constituency coordinator positions in several seats in Selangor after Bersatu signs a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with menteri besar Amirudin Shari's administration, says a source.

The source from Bersatu said the CSA was already in the final stage, with the Perikatan Nasional (PN) component's assemblymen to remain on the opposition bench in the state assembly while obtaining "backbencher status".
The source said Bersatu assemblymen would then be roped into state executive council committees, district offices and local councils.
"All of Umno's constituency coordinators in Bersatu seats will be terminated since they will no longer be required.
"Meanwhile, Umno constituency coordinators in PAS seats will be replaced with coordinators from Bersatu," the source told FMT.
The source said the position of Umno assemblyman Rizam Ismail in the state exco would be discussed by the administration after the CSA is signed.
FMT has reached out to Amirudin's office for comment.
Constituency coordinators are only appointed in opposition-held seats to coordinate and manage the state government's development funds in these areas.
This is because opposition assemblymen in Selangor are not given access to constituency development funds from the state government.
This development comes amid worsening ties between Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional, especially after the latter formed alliances with PN in the Negeri Sembilan and Melaka elections.
While Bersatu is a PN component, it appears to be on the verge of leaving the coalition it founded following a fallout with PAS, which chairs PN.
Last month, Amirudin said Bersatu assemblymen in Selangor would sign a CSA with his administration before the state budget is tabled, with the terms being finalised.
Six Bersatu MPs have similarly signed a CSA with the PH-led federal government, granting them access to constituency development funds.

The 56-member Selangor assembly comprises 32 assemblymen from PH, 11 from Bersatu, 10 from PAS, two from Umno and one independent. However, not all of Bersatu's assemblymen are aligned with the current leadership.
44c6fc1de9854d1e: PETALING JAYA: Umno dijangka kehilangan jawatan penyelaras DUN di beberapa kawasan di Selangor selepas Bersatu memeterai perjanjian keyakinan dan perbekalan (CSA) dengan pentadbiran Menteri Besar Amirudin Shari, menurut satu sumber.

Sumber daripada Bersatu itu berkata CSA berkenaan kini di peringkat akhir, dengan wakil rakyat komponen Perikatan Nasional (PN) itu akan kekal di bangku pembangkang dalam DUN negeri, tetapi diberikan 'status wakil rakyat penyokong kerajaan'.
Sumber itu berkata wakil rakyat Bersatu kemudian akan dilantik menganggotai jawatankuasa majlis mesyuarat kerajaan negeri (MMKN), pejabat daerah dan pihak berkuasa tempatan (PBT).

"Semua penyelaras DUN Umno akan ditamatkan memandangkan semua Adun di kawasan Bersatu tidak diperlukan lagi. Penyelaras di kawasan PAS akan digantikan dengan penyelaras daripada Bersatu,” kata sumber itu kepada FMT.
Sumber itu menambah, kedudukan Adun Umno Rizam Ismai, dalam MMKN akan dibincangkan oleh pentadbiran negeri selepas CSA dimeterai.
FMT sudah menghubungi pejabat menteri besar Selangor Amirudin Shari untuk mendapatkan ulasan.
Penyelaras DUN hanya dilantik di kawasan yang dikuasai pembangkang bagi menyelaras dan menguruskan peruntukan pembangunan kerajaan negeri di kawasan berkenaan.
Ini kerana Adun pembangkang di Selangor tidak mendapat akses kepada peruntukan pembangunan DUN daripada kerajaan negeri.
Perkembangan ini berlaku ketika hubungan antara Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan Barisan Nasional (BN) semakin tegang, khususnya selepas BN menjalin kerjasama dengan PN dalam PRN Negeri Sembilan dan Melaka.
Walaupun Bersatu merupakan komponen PN, parti itu dilihat semakin hampir meninggalkan gabungan yang diasaskannya susulan keretakan hubungan dengan PAS, yang mempengerusikan PN.
Bulan lalu, Amirudin berkata Adun Bersatu di Selangor akan memeterai CSA dengan pentadbirannya sebelum belanjawan negeri dibentangkan, dengan syarat-syarat perjanjian itu sedang dimuktamadkan.
Enam Ahli Parlimen Bersatu turut memeterai CSA dengan kerajaan persekutuan pimpinan PH, sekali gus membolehkan mereka mendapat akses kepada peruntukan pembangunan kawasan masing-masing.
DUN Selangor yang mempunyai 56 kerusi terdiri daripada 32 Adun PH, 11 Bersatu, 10 PAS dan dua Umno. Bagaimanapun, tidak semua Adun Bersatu sehaluan dengan kepimpinan semasa parti itu.

b9f04e041f86ec64: Persidangan Perubahan Iklim Pertubuhan Bangsa-bangsa Bersatu ke-31 (COP31) berlangsung pada 9 hingga 20 Nov 2026 di Antalya, Turki, dengan penyertaan pemimpin negara, menteri, pakar alam sekitar dan pertubuhan antarabangsa.

Persidangan di bawah Konvensyen Rangka Kerja PBB mengenai Perubahan Iklim (UNFCCC) ini merupakan platform rundingan global bagi memperkukuh pelaksanaan Perjanjian Paris, khususnya usaha mengehadkan pemanasan global kepada 1.5°C, mengurangkan pelepasan gas rumah kaca, mempercepat peralihan tenaga bersih serta meningkatkan pembiayaan dan teknologi iklim.
Malaysia menyertai COP31 melalui delegasi diketuai Menteri Sumber Asli dan Kelestarian Alam, Arthur Joseph Kurup, yang menyampaikan Kenyataan Negara pada 17 Nov.

Dalam persidangan tersebut, Arthur memainkan peranan penting mengetengahkan kepentingan negara membangun, khususnya dengan menggesa negara maju meningkatkan bantuan berbentuk geran bagi melindungi hutan dan biodiversiti, memperkukuh pemindahan teknologi serta memastikan pembiayaan iklim yang adil dan mudah diakses.

Beliau turut menegaskan bahawa tindakan iklim antarabangsa mestilah mengambil kira prinsip tanggungjawab bersama tetapi berbeza (common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities, CBDR-RC). Pendirian ini mencerminkan usaha diplomasi Malaysia untuk mengimbangi tanggungjawab memelihara alam sekitar dengan hak negara membangun meneruskan pembangunan demi meningkatkan taraf hidup rakyat.
Gesaan beliau menimbulkan persoalan asas tentang keadilan iklim. Apabila dunia mendapat manfaat daripada hutan tropika yang kekal terpelihara, siapakah yang patut menanggung kos menjaganya?

Panel Antara Kerajaan mengenai Perubahan Iklim (IPCC) meletakkan pengurangan penebangan dan kemerosotan hutan antara langkah mitigasi yang paling berkesan. Hutan tropika menyimpan karbon, mengekalkan habitat dan melindungi kawasan tadahan air. Faedahnya melangkaui sempadan negara yang memeliharanya. Namun begitu, kos rondaan, penguatkuasaan, pemulihan habitat dan pencegahan kebakaran perlu dibayar setiap tahun oleh kerajaan dan masyarakat setempat. Apabila kerajaan memilih untuk melindungi sesuatu kawasan, keputusan itu juga boleh mengehadkan hasil yang boleh diperoleh daripada pembalakan atau penukaran guna tanah.

Negara membangun perlu membiayai sekolah, klinik, bekalan air dan infrastruktur di samping menyediakan pekerjaan. Hutan yang dilindungi turut menyokong pembangunan dengan menjaga bekalan air dan membantu mengurangkan risiko bencana.

Cabarannya ialah manfaat ini jarang menghasilkan aliran tunai yang boleh digunakan untuk membayar balik pinjaman. Geran membolehkan kerja pemuliharaan berjalan tanpa menambah hutang awam, khususnya bagi perlindungan kawasan tadahan, pemulihan gambut dan pengawasan kawasan perlindungan.

Penilaian Jawatankuasa Tetap Kewangan UNFCCC menganggarkan bahawa pada 2023–2024, 57% pembiayaan iklim awam dua hala disalurkan sebagai pinjaman dan 38% sebagai geran. Komposisi ini penting apabila menilai sejauh mana pembiayaan membantu negara penerima.

Perjanjian Paris, menerusi Artikel 9, menetapkan bahawa negara maju menyediakan sumber kewangan bagi membantu negara membangun dalam mitigasi dan adaptasi. Artikel itu turut mengiktiraf keperluan sumber awam dan geran untuk adaptasi. Gesaan Arthur memberi tumpuan kepada kegunaan yang jelas bagi geran tersebut, iaitu melindungi hutan dan biodiversiti.

Sasaran 19 Kerangka Biodiversiti Global Kunming–Montreal menetapkan sasaran aliran pembiayaan biodiversiti antarabangsa sekurang-kurangnya USD30 bilion setahun menjelang 2030. Sasaran itu merangkumi pelbagai bentuk pembiayaan. Penyumbang wajar melaporkan secara terbuka bahagian yang diberikan sebagai geran, tempoh komitmen dan jumlah yang benar-benar diterima supaya kemajuan dapat dinilai berdasarkan dana yang sampai kepada penerima.

Arthur meletakkan gesaan Malaysia dalam kerangka tanggungjawab bersama tetapi berbeza serta keupayaan masing-masing. Prinsip ini mengiktiraf tanggungjawab semua negara untuk bertindak, dengan negara maju mengambil peranan utama. Konvensyen Iklim PBB juga mengiktiraf hak negara untuk memajukan pembangunan mampan dan meminta keadaan khusus negara membangun diberi pertimbangan sewajarnya.
Atas asas ini, tuntutan supaya negara membangun meningkatkan perlindungan hutan mesti disertai pembiayaan yang boleh diakses dan pemindahan teknologi yang membantu mereka melaksanakannya.

Arthur turut membawa isu perdagangan ke dalam perbincangan dengan merujuk Artikel 3.5 Konvensyen. Peruntukan itu menyatakan langkah iklim, termasuk langkah unilateral, tidak seharusnya menjadi alat diskriminasi sewenang-wenangnya atau sekatan perdagangan terselindung.

Implikasinya nyata bagi pengeluar kecil. Jika syarat kebolehkesanan baharu dikenakan, mereka memerlukan masa, kepakaran dan pembiayaan untuk mematuhinya. Negara maju perlu mengambil kira kos pematuhan ini supaya pekebun kecil dapat memenuhi piawaian alam sekitar sambil mengekalkan akses pasaran dan pendapatan.

Di sesi menteri D-8, Arthur mengulangi desakan agar negara maju menunaikan komitmen pembiayaan iklim. Beliau turut menyokong pembangunan Pelan Hala Tuju Iklim dan Alam Sekitar D-8 bagi 2027–2030 serta penyertaan Malaysia dalam kumpulan kerja teknikal.

Melalui kerjasama ini, Malaysia boleh membangunkan projek bersama dalam pemulihan ekosistem, berkongsi kaedah pemantauan hutan dan menambah baik permohonan pembiayaan. Arthur membawa tuntutan Malaysia ke rundingan global sambil membina kerjasama pelaksanaan sesama negara membangun.

Arthur melaporkan 54.40% keluasan negara berada di bawah litupan hutan dan pokok. Kerajaan persekutuan memperuntukkan RM250 juta melalui Ecological Fiscal Transfer pada 2026 untuk menyokong usaha pemuliharaan negeri. Geran antarabangsa boleh memperkukuh usaha ini dengan membiayai pemulihan hutan asli, penyambungan koridor hidupan liar dan pemantauan jangka panjang.

Gesaan Malaysia di COP31 melalui kepimpinan Arthur membawa mesej yang jelas kepada masyarakat antarabangsa bahawa tanggungjawab melindungi hutan dan menangani perubahan iklim tidak boleh dibebankan secara tidak seimbang kepada negara membangun.

Hutan tropika bukan sekadar khazanah sesebuah negara, tetapi turut memberikan manfaat kepada seluruh dunia. Oleh itu, kos pemeliharaannya sewajarnya dikongsi secara adil. Negara maju tidak boleh sekadar menuntut supaya hutan negara membangun terus dipelihara, sedangkan bantuan yang diberikan tidak mencukupi atau hanya menambahkan beban hutang mereka.
Penulis ialah pensyarah di Pusat Pengajian Kerajaan (SoG) Universiti Utara Malaysia.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
46e6624629d3c2eb: TANGKAK: A misunderstanding over messages in a WhatsApp group is believed to have led to a Form Two student being beaten up by three male students at a secondary school here.
In the incident at 8am on Nov 13, the victim was allegedly kicked and punched repeatedly in the classroom by the three 15-year-old students.
The incident came to light after a video of the assault went viral on social media.
Tangkak police chief Superintendent Mohd Roslan Talib said police received a report on the incident at 12.09am on Nov 14.
He said the victim sought treatment at the Sultanah Fatimah Specialist Hospital (HPSF) in Muar after sustaining injuries to several parts of his body.
"Medical examinations found the victim suffered injuries to his head, chest, abdomen and left arm.
"Acting on the report, police identified and arrested the three male students suspected of involvement in the incident.
"Initial investigations found the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a WhatsApp group chat, which sparked dissatisfaction among the students," he said in a statement.
Roslan said all three suspects admitted their involvement during questioning.
The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.
"Police view any bullying and violence, especially involving school students, seriously.
"Resorting to force to resolve misunderstandings not only causes injury, but also endangers the victim's safety.
"Parents and schools are urged to remain vigilant over their children's behaviour and social circles, and not take any bullying complaints lightly," he said.
5b290a4356dab46c: KUALA TERENGGANU: Two men suspected of robbing a goldsmith shop in Batu Enam, Gong Badak, of jewellery worth RM500,000 have been remanded for seven days to assist police investigations.
Magistrate Nur Akmal Mohd Bakri issued the remand order today, allowing the suspects to be held from Nov 19 to 25.
The robbery took place at 10.45am on Nov 12, when the two men, wearing helmets and face coverings, entered the Permata Al-Idrus goldsmith shop.
One of the suspects, armed with a parang, entered the inner section of the shop while his accomplice kept watch and monitored the employees.
All employees fled to the back of the premises for safety.
The suspects then grabbed three trays of jewellery worth an estimated RM500,000 before fleeing in a white Perodua Axia.

The case is being investigated under Section 395 of the Penal Code for gang robbery, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping, and Section 397 for armed robbery, which provides for imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
61c16f1753cf2ba1: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johoreans can expect more financial assistance, housing support and cost-of-living relief under the state's RM3.07 billion Budget 2027 tabled today.

Themed Johor Maju, Rakyat Sejahtera (Johor advances, people prosper), the budget outlines 284 commitments targeting B40 and M40 households, entrepreneurs, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), farmers and the agriculture sector.

Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said Johor will channel RM1.53 billion towards development projects next year, accounting for almost half of its total expenditure, to ensure economic growth translates into better living conditions.
"The allocation is part of the 284 commitments outlined under the six pillars of the Johor Maju framework in Budget 2027.
"Johor will also channel its growing revenue towards helping more vulnerable groups, including poor families, orphans, people with disabilities (PwDs) and senior citizens.

"The government I lead will continue to work wholeheartedly, serve and care for the people regardless of their political background, race or religion. We will serve everyone," he said when tabling the budget at the state assembly sitting at Dewan Persidangan, Bangunan Sultan Ismail, here today.
For 2027, Johor projected revenue of RM3.08 billion against expenditure of RM3.07 billion, resulting in an estimated surplus of RM2.33 million.
Onn Hafiz said state revenue had reached RM2.8 billion as of this morning, representing 110 per cent of the original estimate for 2026.
He said he was confident that Johor's revenue would surpass RM3 billion for the first time in the state's history by the end of this year.
"This is the Johor we want — economically advanced, prosperous and with a happy Bangsa Johor," he said.

8e33b0b39a5f65f8: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected construction sites in South Hamgyong Province on Tuesday and Wednesday, as well as a naval university, state news agency KCNA reported on Thursday.
His visits came as some analysts speculated he might meet US president Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen this week.

During Wednesday's visit to the Kim Jong Suk Naval University, Kim said its importance was "remarkably increasing" and that the navy "is evolving into the high-tech service and multi-functional combined army branch."
Kim, who also cited a changing security environment and mounting challenges, has repeatedly stressed the importance of naval forces and the modernisation of the navy.
Earlier this month, he inspected the construction of a naval base and a new warship, believed by analysts to be its latest cruiser.
North Korea has not given any public response to Trump's remark on Monday that he might meet Kim in China this week.

Kim's visit to the construction sites in the eastern province of the country could indicate the North Korean leader did not intend to attend Apec, said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at South Korea's Kyungnam University.

The prospect of Trump visiting Pyongyang on his return from Apec also appeared low, with no sign so far of activity by US security personnel in North Korea, said Yang Moo-jin, a ​professor emeritus at ⁠the University of North Korean Studies.
A delegation led by a close aide to Kim returned by private plane on Wednesday after visiting Russia, KCNA also reported.
Jo Yong Won, a member of North Korea's ruling Workers' Party Political Bureau, met with Valentina Matvienko, chairwoman of the Federation Council of Russia, KCNA said, citing Russian media reports.

Matvienko told Jo that "Russia will always cherish the memory of bravery and heroism displayed by DPRK combatants," KCNA reported, using the acronym for North Korea's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.
North Korea has ​sent about 14,000 ​to 15,000 ⁠troops to support Russia's war in Ukraine since 2024, according to Ukrainian and South ​Korean estimates.
Jo also met with Russian President Vladimir Putin, KCNA reported on Wednesday.
7f6454bae262b735: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has strengthened its position in the aviation industry after being recognised internationally for its role in supporting the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) sector.

The awards recognise its onboard travel experience and range of solutions tailored to the needs of event organisers.
Beyond its MICE services, Malaysia Airlines offers extensive destination connectivity, onboard comfort, dining options and flexible booking arrangements to cater to different travel needs.
SUPPORTING MICE TRAVEL
For organisers managing events involving delegates from different cities and countries, coordinating group travel can be challenging.
Through MHcorporate EVENTS, Malaysia Airlines offers a dedicated service to simplify travel arrangements.
This includes preferential fares, special group rates and the flexibility for delegates to travel up to seven days before and after an event, whether attending conferences or exhibitions.
The service also caters to specialised group movements, including concert tours, artists' entourages and festival-related events.
Organisers can also benefit from the airline's network of more than 70 destinations worldwide, complemented by sister airline Firefly's regional network.
This helps connect attendees from across Asia and beyond.
CONNECTIVITY ACROSS DESTINATIONS
With its extensive network, Malaysia Airlines connects passengers to destinations across different regions while helping organisers bring international delegates together.
Its connectivity through Firefly further expands travel options across the region, catering to both smaller groups and larger-scale movements.
COMFORT THROUGHOUT THE JOURNEY
Passengers travelling aboard Malaysia Airlines' A330neo can enjoy a range of onboard features designed to enhance comfort and convenience throughout their journey.
Business Class
• Fully flat beds for a more comfortable rest. • Privacy doors and direct aisle access. • 17.3-inch 4K entertainment screens. • Built-in wireless charging.
Economy Class
• 13.3-inch 4K entertainment screens. • Extra legroom in selected seats.
Passengers in both cabins can also enjoy complimentary unlimited Wi-Fi, allowing them to stay connected throughout their journey.
DINING WITH A LOCAL TOUCH
The onboard dining experience features a rotating menu of regional and destination-inspired dishes, offering passengers a selection of meals throughout their journey.
Business Class passengers on eligible flights can also use the Chef-on-Call service to pre-order selected signature dishes before departure.
GREATER FLEXIBILITY WHEN BOOKING
Travel plans do not always go as expected. Malaysia Airlines therefore offers booking options designed to give passengers greater flexibility.
These include:
• Easy refunds: Passengers whose visa applications are unsuccessful may be eligible for a refund, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

• MH Flex fares: These offer unlimited rebooking, subject to any applicable fare difference, as well as the option of travelling earlier on the same day, subject to availability. Passengers also enjoy priority check-in, boarding and baggage handling.
From supporting international MICE events to providing greater comfort, connectivity and booking flexibility, Malaysia Airlines offers a range of services to enhance the overall travel experience.
For more information on Malaysia Airlines' services and MHcorporate EVENTS, visit the official Malaysia Airlines website.

656df5777e2cb3c1: PETALING JAYA: Kekuatan undi Melayu Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) di Kota Melaka dilihat hampir mencapai tahap maksimum, kata dua penganalisis yang melihat usaha merampas kerusi Parlimen itu daripada DAP pada PRU16 sukar tanpa sokongan tambahan pengundi bukan Melayu.

Hisommudin Bakar dan Lau Zhe Wei senada undi Melayu sahaja belum cukup untuk mengubah keputusan di Kota Melaka memandangkan pengundi Cina membentuk 52% pemilih, dengan kira-kira 85% daripada mereka masih menyokong Pakatan Harapan (PH).

Hisommudin yang juga pengarah eksekutif Ilham Centre berkata sokongan pengundi Melayu kepada BN-PN mencecah sekitar 77% pada PRN Melaka 14 Nov lalu, dengan kadar keluar mengundi golongan itu sekitar 82%.
"Kekuatan BN-PN dalam kalangan pengundi Melayu juga hampir mencapai tahap maksimum," katanya kepada FMT.

Hisommudin berkata calon BN-PN perlu mengekalkan sokongan Melayu sekitar 85% menjelang PRU16 dan meningkatkan sokongan pengundi Cina kepada sekurang-kurangnya 15% hingga 20%, berbanding sekitar 4% hingga 7% yang diperoleh MCA dan PN ketika ini.

Lau dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia (UIAM) pula berkata: “Jika pengundi Cina terus kekal bersama PH, kerusi Parlimen Kota Melaka yang mempunyai lebih ramai pengundi Cina berkemungkinan besar akan terus berada dalam tangan gabungan itu.”
Kerusi yang pernah diwakili Lim Kit Siang dan Lim Guan Eng itu hanya terlepas daripada DAP untuk satu penggal apabila dimenangi MCA pada PRU 2004, sebelum dirampas semula pada 2008.
Pada PRN lalu, Umno mengekalkan Duyong dan Telok Mas dengan majoriti terkumpul 21,154 undi, berbanding 26,633 undi majoriti DAP di Kesidang, Kota Laksamana dan Bandar Hilir.
Keputusan itu menyaksikan PH masih mendahului BN-PN dengan kelebihan keseluruhan 5,479 undi di lima DUN berkenaan.
Sebelum ini, Ketua Umno Kota Melaka Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman mendakwa jurang itu membuka peluang BN-PN merampas kerusi Parlimen berkenaan pada PRU16.
Beliau merujuk 56,455 undi diraih PH berbanding 50,976 undi BN-PN, jauh lebih kecil daripada majoriti 46,420 undi diperoleh PH pada PRU15.

Bagaimanapun, Hisommudin berkata jurang yang mengecil itu turut dipengaruhi penurunan kadar keluar mengundi pengundi Cina kepada sekitar 57%, berbanding 70% pada PRU15, selain 5,818 undi yang diperoleh Bersama.
“Malah, jurang undi boleh melebar semula kepada sekitar 14,000 sekiranya pola keluar mengundi pada PRU15 berulang.

"Keputusan PRN tidak boleh diterjemahkan secara langsung sebagai petunjuk kemenangan BN-PN pada PRU16," katanya, sambil menegaskan kedua-dua pilihan raya mempunyai dinamika berbeza dan Kota Melaka masih merupakan kubu kuat DAP.
Mengulas watak politik yang berpotensi ditampilkan gabungan BN-PN untuk mencabar DAP dan PH, Hisommudin dan Lau senada Adun Duyong, Noor Helmy Abdul Halem mampu menggalasnya.

“Jika Umno letak calon seperti Helmy, membuka peluang kepada Umno untuk memenangi Kota Melaka sekiranya peralihan sokongan pengundi Cina seperti yang berlaku di Duyong turut berlaku di peringkat Parlimen,” kata Lau merujuk kemenangan Helmy dengan majoriti 10,040 undi.
89e26074ac22e971: PETALING JAYA: An analyst has cautioned that the proposal to revive the Barisan Alternatif (BA) alliance without DAP risks the double whammy of a split in Malay votes and the loss of non-Malay support.

Syaza Shukri of International Islamic University Malaysia said the scenario would leave PAS with no strong reason to ditch Umno, which the Islamic party is courting for a pact in the 16th general election.

Syaza said an Umno pact would be far more beneficial for PAS due to the potential of garnering up to 80% of the Malay vote, and as proven by the dominant victories of the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) alliance in the Negeri Sembilan and Melaka elections.
Working with PKR under BA would mean PAS having to compete with Umno-BN for Malay votes once again, she added.
"So the Malay votes will be split, while the non-Malay votes will go to DAP," she told FMT.

In the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast, former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin said a revival of the BA alliance between PKR, PAS and DAP could "save" Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim from the political onslaught posed by the BN-PN alliance.
He said Pakatan Harapan (PH) was in desperate need of a Malay bloc in the coalition, and that PAS could fill that role.
Co-host Shahril Hamdan added that the only way to convince PAS to agree would be to remove DAP from the alliance.

BA was formed in 1999 at the height of the Reformasi movement following Anwar's sacking as deputy prime minister, with Parti Keadilan Nasional (now PKR), DAP, PAS and Parti Rakyat Malaysia joining hands.
Syaza said one common denominator that could be the basis of a BA revival was the anti-corruption agenda, which the alliance championed in 1999.

"Right now, both PAS and Anwar are linked to BN, which has corruption scandals of its own. It's possible they would both distance themselves from BN (because of the scandals) and work together," she said.
Seats, oil royalty could win PAS over

Universiti Teknologi Malaysia's Mazlan Ali said PAS would have several reasons to consider working with PH, including the opportunity to contest the lion's share of Malay-majority seats and more Cabinet posts.
Mazlan said an Umno-PAS pact would face the major hurdle of reaching an agreeable seat distribution, since both Malay-Muslim parties eye the same type of constituency.

"However, if PAS works with Anwar, PAS would definitely be allocated more Malay-majority areas because Anwar and PH would be willing to make way for PAS there," he said, citing PH's strength among urban, progressive voters.

Mazlan said resolving Kelantan and Terengganu's oil royalty demands could be another strategic motivation, on top of taking advantage of closer ties with Putrajaya to boost development in the two states as well as Kedah.
"Offering oil royalties would definitely attract PAS," he said.
Two days ago, Amanah communications director Khalid Samad appealed to PAS, his former party, to consider ending its cooperation with Umno and backing Anwar's government instead.
Khalid said Amanah could help lead discussions on roping PAS into the government if the Islamic party wanted to join the administration.

Musk was asked about the dispute during a live interview with journalist Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times Dealbook Summit.
Sorkin asked Musk about Zelensky referring to the system being slowed down as "Starshield."
"That's false. I don't want to blow your mind, but Zelensky is not always truthful," Musk said.

When pressed again about whether the system was actually Starshield, Musk said Zelensky "is lying, and what he is actually saying is he wants to use Starlink for military, offensive military operations."
The SpaceX boss said that Starlink had been limited to the maximum highway speed of Ukraine.

"What I'm trying to tell you is Zelensky is actually asking to use the Starlink commercial satellites, and for offensive military actions, and we have declined to do so, as we have declined to do so from the beginning of this conflict. End of story," he added.
961b5babea600536: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lelaki dipercayai penjenayah maut dalam insiden berbalas tembakan dengan polis di Ipoh, Perak awal pagi tadi.

Pengarah Jabatan Siasatan Jenayah Bukit Aman, M Kumar, berkata anggota polis sebelum itu menahan sebuah kenderaan di Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan ketika menjalankan rondaan cegah jenayah sebelum suspek keluar dan cuba melarikan diri.
Katanya, suspek melepaskan beberapa das tembakan ke arah polis, yang kemudiannya membalas tembakan untuk menyelamatkan diri sehingga tiada ancaman keselamatan.
"Suspek warga tempatan disahkan meninggal dunia pada 3.40 pagi. Sepucuk pistol ditemukan berhampiran suspek,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Kumar berkata kes terbabit disiasat mengikut Seksyen 307 Kanun Keseksaan kerana cubaan membunuh dan Seksyen 3 Akta Senjata Api kerana melepaskan tembakan dengan niat menyebabkan kematian atau kecederaan kepada seseorang.
Beliau berkata siasatan masih dijalankan dan orang ramai diminta tidak membuat sebarang spekulasi berhubung kejadian itu.
Tambahnya, satu sidang media akan diadakan di IPK Perak pada 3 petang ini bagi mendedahkan maklumat lanjut mengenai kejadian berkenaan.
e804070f1d27d731: KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts have raised their earnings forecasts for UEM Sunrise Bhd after the property developer posted stronger-than-expected third-quarter results, supported by higher joint venture contributions and improved property development earnings.

The group's net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), surged 163.6 per cent to RM48.75 million from RM18.49 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 13.7 per cent to RM474.88 million.

The stronger performance prompted research firms to revise their earnings projections upwards, with analysts expecting the group to sustain its momentum into the final quarter, supported by higher contributions from joint ventures, property sales and land transactions.

Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) raised its FY26 earnings forecast by 22.9 per cent, mainly to account for higher contributions from joint ventures and associates, while Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) revised its FY26 to FY28 earnings estimates upwards by an average of 60 per cent after factoring in stronger sales and changes to billing assumptions.

CIMB Securities, meanwhile, raised its FY26 core profit forecast by 72 per cent to RM192 million, reflecting higher joint venture earnings and an estimated RM66 million net gain from the disposal of the Jalan Ampang land.
HLIB expects UEM Sunrise to record another strong quarter in Q4 FY26, supported by the recognition of the Jalan Ampang land sale, which it estimates could contribute about RM66 million in net gain.

The property developer has also surpassed its FY26 sales target of RM1.3 billion, securing RM1.94 billion in sales in the first nine months of the year, while its launches recorded a gross development value of RM2.64 billion, exceeding its FY26 launch target of RM2.2 billion.

The group's nine-month net profit rose 82.1 per cent to RM111.8 million, while revenue increased 11.8 per cent to RM1.43 billion, with stronger contributions from associates and joint ventures, particularly land sale transactions.

UEM Sunrise also declared a special dividend of 1.53 sen per share, which HLIB viewed as a positive surprise, supported by proceeds from the RM415 million Jalan Ampang land sale that strengthened its cash position.
Despite the earnings upgrades, analysts differed in their valuations of the stock, with HLIB maintaining a target price of 92 sen, PublicInvest at 60 sen, and CIMB at 72 sen.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call, citing progress in the group's development pipeline and land monetisation efforts, while PublicInvest reiterated "Trading Buy".

CIMB also maintained its "Buy" recommendation but lowered its target price to 72 sen from 83 sen, citing uncertainties surrounding US AI chip export restrictions that could delay industrial land monetisation, as well as the upcoming general election.
b6cde8d14ac06303: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's vehicle sales rose three per cent to 673,412 units in the first 10 months of 2026, from 655,327 units a year earlier, despite a weaker performance in October.
The Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA) said total industry volume fell seven per cent year-on-year to 70,519 units in October, compared with 75,991 units in the same month last year.
Passenger vehicle sales declined seven per cent to 65,362 units, while commercial vehicle sales dropped nine per cent to 5,157 units.

However, sales improved 1.3 per cent month-on-month from 69,609 units in September, supported by a four per cent increase in passenger vehicle sales and an eight per cent rise in commercial vehicle sales.
MAA said demand for commercial vehicles had improved, with pick-up sales reaching 3,740 units, the highest monthly volume recorded so far this year.
It added that the government's support through the BUDI Diesel programme had also helped pave the way for a recovery in the commercial vehicle segment.
For the January-October period, passenger vehicle sales increased four per cent to 630,461 units from 606,443 units previously.
In contrast, commercial vehicle sales fell 12 per cent to 42,951 units from 48,884 units.
On the production front, total vehicle output rose three per cent year-on-year to 67,416 units in October.
This brings cumulative production for the first 10 months to 629,623 units, up two per cent from 617,693 units previously.
Passenger vehicle production increased three per cent to 63,598 units in October, while commercial vehicle output dropped five per cent to 3,818 units.
MAA expects sales momentum to continue into November, supported by a positive economic outlook and year-end promotional campaigns.
ee1c2eda103e04b2: MYANMAR: Myanmar's military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing said on Wednesday his administration was reconsidering the country's relationship with Southeast Asia's regional bloc Asean but would continue discussions with its members.

The former junta chief turned president, whose coup against an elected civilian government in 2021 triggered a nationwide civil war, also told parliament he planned to hold a peace conference in February, with the aim of ending fighting within his five-year term.
The state-run Global New Light of Myanmar newspaper reported on Thursday that the conference would be held in February 2028.

The position of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, which met this week without including Myanmar, appeared to disappoint Min Aung Hlaing, who has been pushing for re-engagement with the bloc.

Asean leaders said in a statement on Sunday that they may consider gradually restoring Myanmar's full political representation within the group if the country makes progress on their longstanding plan to resolve its crisis.
"They are imposing such pressure only on our country," Min Aung Hlaing said.
"There was never pressure placed on or indignity shown towards an Asean member before. But with Myanmar, they are doing that."

Since he became president in April following a widely criticised election dominated by an army-backed party, Min Aung Hlaing has visited several Asean member countries, including Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam. Nearly half the bloc's 11 members have stepped up bilateral engagement since the election.

"For Myanmar and Asean to resume normal relations, we will take into consideration Myanmar's stance and the intentions of Asean member countries. We will continue to discuss with Asean member countries," he said.
The foreign ministry of the Philippines, the current Asean chair, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Min Aung Hlaing's remarks.

At their annual summit held in Manila, Asean leaders said they had agreed to pursue a "calibrated engagement" through a "phased and progress-based" approach if Myanmar makes "sustained and concrete" progress on the bloc's proposed plan, known as the five-point consensus.

The five-point consensus, adopted soon after the 2021 coup, calls for an immediate end to violence there and the launch of constructive dialogue among all parties, while also offering Asean mediation and humanitarian assistance.
But fighting has raged on in Myanmar, where the military is locked in conflict with an array of armed groups. More than 100,000 people have died and millions have been displaced.
Despite calls for calm, the Myanmar military has stepped up a deadly bombing campaign in parts of the country, including multiple airstrikes that have killed large numbers of civilians.
Min Aung Hlaing offered few details about his proposed peace conference, which would be the first since he became president. Previous peace talk efforts have produced limited results.
5c30e12d2d718846: PETALING JAYA: A man was killed in a shootout with police in Ipoh, Perak, at around 2.30am today, says Bukit Aman's criminal investigation department.
Its director, M Kumar, said officers stopped a vehicle at Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan during a crime prevention patrol, and the suspect exited it in an attempt to escape.
The suspect also fired several gunshots at the officers, who returned fire in self-defence "until there was no threat to their safety".
"The suspect, a Malaysian, was confirmed dead at the scene around 3.40am. A pistol was found near the suspect," Kumar said in a statement.
The case is being probed under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder and Section 3 of the Firearms Act for discharging a firearm with intent to harm or murder someone.
Kumar said the case is still under investigation and urged the public against speculating on it.
He added that a press conference will be held at the Perak police headquarters at 3pm today where more details on the incident will be disclosed.

667a39657cef32ec: KUALA LUMPUR: The United Nations refugee agency's Malaysian office has stopped its registration and documentation activities following a decision by the government to build its own system for managing asylum seekers.

The UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said it fully supported the government's efforts to strengthen its asylum management framework and remains engaged on a transition roadmap to ensure continued protection for refugees.
"The proposed roadmap emphasises appropriate safeguards, effective communication and collaboration among all relevant stakeholders," it said in a statement.
Malaysia is not a party to the UN refugee convention and regards asylum seekers as illegal migrants.
UNHCR previously registered, documented and provided support to refugees in Malaysia, mostly persecuted Rohingya Muslims from Myanmar.
The UN's top court is set to rule on Thursday whether Myanmar's 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya amounted to genocide.

Rights groups have criticised Malaysia's refugee registration programme, citing a lack of transparency and adequate safeguards. The government has said it allows refugee data to be better managed, including for identity verification and monitoring.
UNHCR said it would provide technical advice and cooperation throughout the transition and continue other activities including resettlement and support to refugees with urgent protection needs.
4942e18640df2fc5: SINGAPORE: The US dollar hovered near a 19-month high on Thursday after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Fed official pointed to further interest rate hikes.

The Australian dollar slipped to a 10-month low after soft jobs data, reaching US$0.6692, the lowest level since January. The country's employment fell for a second-straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that Australian rates have likely peaked.

A broadly strong dollar also pressured the euro to near its lowest since April 2025, last trading at US$1.0977, while sterling languished near a one-month low at US$1.3152. The yen was little changed at 159.39, hovering around the closely watched 160 level.

Driving the greenback's strength were hawkish signals from the Fed. Officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their Oct 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller reinforced that tone, saying the central bank should either raise rates by 50 basis points in December or signal faster hikes in 2027.

Fed hawkishness has kept the greenback bid even as technology shares wobble. Chip bellwether Nvidia fell overnight even after beating on revenue and guidance amid uncertainties caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure as CEO last week following his admission of extramarital affairs.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the dollar supported," OCBC analysts said, adding that a deeper downgrade to expectations for AI capital expenditure would challenge that support by pushing down US real yields and weakening equity inflows.

Treasuries rallied overnight, led by longer-dated notes after a solid 20-year auction, with the 10-year yield down about 4 basis points to 5.06%. They were little moved in early trade on Thursday. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

"Falling oil prices helped ease some inflation concerns, while weakness in US equities and worries about economic growth may have encouraged some safe-haven buying in Treasuries," Dilin Wu, research strategist at Pepperstone said.

Oil prices settled down more than 1% on Wednesday after US crude and fuel inventories posted larger-than-expected rises, according to the Energy Information Administration, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.
Gold stabilised US$3,743 an ounce after a sharp selloff overnight on hawkish Fed signals.
The dollar index was roughly flat at 103.81 in early Asia trade, hovering near its highest level since April 2025.
Investors are also bracing for the stock market debut of Anthropic as a test for AI sentiment, while watching a cluster of high-stakes meetings between world leaders on Thursday.

US President Donald Trump will cap his Asia trip on Thursday with an unprecedented meeting with Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, pressing his ambitions for nuclear arms control even as Beijing resists making the issue a centerpiece of the gathering.
411c7fb95abaead6: TOKYO: Kozo Tashima said on Wednesday he was prepared to hold talks with rival French candidate Philippe Diallo about their bids to become FIFA president.

The 68-year-old Tashima, who has served on the FIFA Council and is the Japan Football Association's honorary president, will attempt to unseat current FIFA chief Gianni Infantino in the March election.
Infantino is under pressure after his aborted plan to open up FIFA's premium competitions, such as the World Cup, to private investors.
Tashima said he wanted to make FIFA a "more trusted organisation" after Japan's FA officially submitted his candidacy for president of world football's governing body ahead of the Wednesday deadline.
Tashima also said he wanted to bring Japan's "strong sense of ethics" to football's top job.
Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation, was a late entrant to the race this week and has the backing of European football's governing body UEFA.
Tashima gave a cautious welcome to the Frenchman's suggestion of talks.
"Mr. Diallo has indicated that he wishes to speak with me. It's clear we need to talk," Tashima said in an interview with French sports daily L'Equipe.

"But we must consider one thing: is the mere fact that our programmes are similar, enough for us to decide to work together, or unite? Or should we think tactically, asking what the most effective strategy would be to defeat Infantino?"
Earlier, Tashima, who has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands, set out the basis of his bid.
"We will share with the world the importance of fair play, respect and integrity – the core values at the very heart of football and of sport itself," he said in a statement released by the JFA.

"With a strong sense of mission and firm resolve, I will take on this challenge so that FIFA can become a healthier and more trusted organisation and contribute even more to the further development of football worldwide."
In opposing Infantino, Tashima is going against his own confederation after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election.
Tashima was JFA president from 2016 to 2024 and also served on the AFC executive committee.
Infantino also has the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.
Diallo said Tuesday he has support from countries beyond Europe.
Swiss former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega has also stated his intention to run for president.

Arsene Wenger, the French former Arsenal manager and FIFA's current chief of global football development, had at one point been seen as a potential candidate who could get Europe's backing but he will not stand.
The election will take place at the FIFA Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.
FIFA has a total of 211 member associations, with each having one vote in the presidential election. - AFP

486aa32420be3c86: KUALA LUMPUR: Noor Kumalasari remains a towering figure in Malaysian entertainment, celebrated for her brilliance in acting, singing and modelling throughout the 1970s and 1980s.
Now 70, the veteran star has long stepped away from the limelight in favour of a quieter, spiritual life, and harbours no regrets.

"Praise be to God, there is no feeling of regret. So far, there are no new artistic projects, though people still call me for interviews," she said, noting that her decision to wear the hijab happened gradually through persistent prayer after returning from the haj.
Despite frequent offers from production houses, the door to the filming set remains firmly shut.
"Those offers do not stir me at all. So far, I have no desire to return to acting," said the veteran artiste.
The younger sister of Anita Sarawak welcomes today's new talent, though she misses the golden era's tangible fan letters and Hari Raya cards.
Steer­ing clear of social media to protect her peace, she avoids Instagram entirely.
"It messes with your head! I also don't have a fan club; at my age, there's no need for all that because the grave is already calling," she joked.
While effortlessly graceful at 70, she candidly acknowledges her diminishing physical strength.
"I have to be guided when going up the stairs for fear of falling. Even at 70, I still want to pretend to walk like a model with style!" she quipped.
Closing the book on her career, the 'Esok Untuk Siapa' actress feels deeply fulfilled and urged mutual respect across generations.
"If there were no older generation, there would be no successors today. We must always respect and support all practitioners, especially the younger ones striving to make their mark."

Ahead of the 35th Malaysian Film Festival (FFM35), the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) celebrated the contributions of veteran artistes Noor Kumalasari, Datuk Yusof Haslam, A.R. Badul, and Norlia Ghani to the local film industry by hosting free screenings of their work.
The FFM35 awards ceremony kicks off at Istana Budaya on Nov 21 at 8.30pm, with a live broadcast on RTM's TV2 and Finas' YouTube channel.
040e6916f52a2264: PETALING JAYA: A DAP leader has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to disclose the status of its investigation into the 2002 Scorpene submarine deal with France.

Wanita DAP legal bureau chief Sangeet Kaur Deo pointed out that new defence deals were signed with French firms yesterday during French president Emmanuel Macron's visit to Malaysia, including a "mid-life upgrade programme" for the navy's Scorpene submarines.
She said the government should know the full dealings and allegations involved in the initial Scorpene deal before entering into fresh agreements with the same companies.
"Moving forward with France cannot mean sweeping the unresolved Scorpene affair under the carpet.
"MACC must state publicly whether the Scorpene investigation is still active, what became of the RM42 million payout lead and whether anyone will be charged.
"If the investigation has been closed, say so, and explain why," she said in a statement.

The incarcerated Najib Razak was defence minister when the deal was signed for two Scorpene-class submarines and one Agosta submarine from French naval dockyards unit DCN, now part of the defence firm Thales, in a deal worth US$1.2 billion.

His associate, Abdul Razak Baginda, acted as an adviser on the deal and was accused of disguising a kickback of more than 114 million euros as "consulting work" by a firm in which he was the largest shareholder.

Two years ago, MACC said its investigation into the procurement of two French Scorpene submarines in 2002 was still ongoing. A source later revealed that the agency received a new lead in its probe, related to RM42 million in payments made by a local company without its board's knowledge.
The RM42 million was said to be part of a RM530 million contract for support services in relation to the purchase of the submarine.
In 2022, Thales was charged with complicity in bribery over Malaysia's purchase of the three submarines.
The deal for the submarines' mid-life upgrade programme was signed yesterday with Thales and Safran.
Sangeet urged the government to explain what due diligence had been carried out before the mid-life upgrade deal was signed with Thales, and if the agreement includes anti-corruption safeguards.

"The government must also state its position on the Scorpene affair, including what it is doing to protect Malaysia’s interests in the French proceedings and to recover any public money that was lost."
ade6390bf9c2fcf6: PETALING JAYA: Seorang pemimpin DAP menggesa Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) mendedahkan status siasatannya berhubung urus niaga pembelian kapal selam Scorpene dari Perancis pada 2002.

Ketua Biro Undang-undang Wanita DAP, Sangeet Kaur Deo, berkata gesaan itu dibuat selepas perjanjian pertahanan baharu dimeterai dengan syarikat Perancis semalam, sempena lawatan Presiden Perancis Emmanuel Macron ke Malaysia, termasuk program 'pemodenan pertengahan hayat' kapal selam Scorpene milik Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia (TLDM).

Sangeet berkata kerajaan perlu mengetahui sepenuhnya urus niaga dan dakwaan berkaitan pembelian kapal selam Scorpene sebelum memeterai perjanjian baharu dengan syarikat sama yang terbabit dalam urus niaga terdahulu.
“Usaha memperkukuh hubungan dengan Perancis tidak boleh bermakna isu Scorpene yang belum selesai disapu ke bawah permaidani.
“SPRM mesti menyatakan secara terbuka sama ada siasatan Scorpene masih berjalan, apakah perkembangan petunjuk berhubung pembayaran RM42 juta itu dan sama ada mana-mana individu akan didakwa.
“Jika siasatan sudah ditutup, nyatakan demikian dan jelaskan sebabnya,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Najib Razak, yang kini dipenjarakan, merupakan menteri pertahanan ketika perjanjian pembelian dua kapal selam kelas Scorpene dan sebuah kapal selam Agosta daripada unit limbungan kapal tentera laut Perancis, DCN — kini sebahagian daripada syarikat pertahanan Thales — dimeterai pada nilai USD1.2 bilion.

Sekutunya, Abdul Razak Baginda, bertindak sebagai penasihat dalam urus niaga itu. Beliau didakwa menyembunyikan bayaran komisen melebihi €114 juta sebagai 'kerja perundingan' oleh sebuah syarikat yang mana beliau merupakan pemegang saham terbesar.

Dua tahun lalu, SPRM berkata siasatannya berhubung pemerolehan dua kapal selam Scorpene dari Perancis pada 2002 masih berjalan. Satu sumber kemudian mendedahkan agensi itu menerima petunjuk baharu dalam siasatannya, berkaitan pembayaran RM42 juta yang dibuat sebuah syarikat tempatan tanpa pengetahuan lembaga pengarahnya.
RM42 juta itu dilaporkan sebahagian daripada kontrak bernilai RM530 juta bagi perkhidmatan sokongan berkaitan pembelian kapal selam berkenaan.
Pada 2022, Thales didakwa atas pertuduhan bersubahat dalam rasuah berhubung pembelian tiga kapal selam oleh Malaysia.
Perjanjian bagi program pemodenan pertengahan hayat kapal selam itu dimeterai semalam dengan Thales dan Safran.

Sangeet menggesa kerajaan menjelaskan usaha penelitian sewajarnya yang dilakukan sebelum perjanjian itu dimeterai dengan Thales, serta sama ada perjanjian berkenaan merangkumi perlindungan antirasuah.

“Kerajaan juga mesti menyatakan pendiriannya berhubung isu Scorpene, termasuk langkah yang diambil untuk melindungi kepentingan Malaysia dalam prosiding di Perancis dan mendapatkan semula wang awam yang mungkin telah hilang.”
eaa81e32e3893026: KUALA LUMPUR: A shortage of operational trains on the Kelana Jaya LRT line is expected to result in longer waiting times and overcrowding on platforms, particularly during peak hours.
Rapid KL said its engineering team is working to increase the number of operational trains as soon as possible to restore service frequency on the line.
"Some trains will temporarily turn back at selected locations to help improve passenger movement and ease congestion at busier stations.
"Passengers are advised to allow extra time for their journeys and follow the latest updates through Rapid KL's official channels," it said in a statement.

Meanwhile, a review of comments on Rapid KL's official Facebook page found that many passengers had expressed dissatisfaction over service disruptions and unusually heavy congestion at several stations, particularly Jelatek LRT station.
Facebook user Muhd Syahmi questioned the decision to abruptly terminate train services at the station, claiming that there had been no apparent technical fault.
"Why did the train service stop at Jelatek? Nothing happened, there was no breakdown, but suddenly passengers were told to get off," he said.
Another user, CZ BC, described a frightening experience when the crowded train he was travelling on made an emergency stop after passing Jelatek station.
"After struggling through the crowd at Jelatek, the train made an emergency stop at Ampang while packed with passengers. I felt as though my arm would break from holding on to the handrail.
"Please, management, look into the current LRT service," the user said.
fbcddf9de2101305: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak will return to Kajang Prison for Friday prayers and counselling on Saturday.
"The Prisons Department has made arrangements for him to perform Friday prayers at the prison surau," a source told Berita Harian.
"The following day, he has a Quran recital class and counselling session scheduled at the prison," said the source, who declined to be named.
Last week, Najib also performed Friday prayers at Kajang Prison.
It was the first time he had left his Jalan Langgak Duta residence after being allowed to serve the remainder of his jail term in the SRC International case under house arrest.
Najib will remain under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
This followed the settlement of his RM50 million fine in the case.
b28fc6e35b6ab63e: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday as market sentiment remained fragile, with no strong buying commitments amid a mixed Wall Street session.
At 9.18 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shed 6.92 points to 1,560.23 from Wednesday’s close of 1,566.73.
The benchmark index opened 6.29 points lower at 1,559.81.
Market breadth was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 243 to 159. A total of 245 counters were unchanged, while 2,175 remained untraded and 14 were suspended.
Turnover stood at 475.73 million units worth RM254.04 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the FBM KLCI slipped to around the 1,565 level as investors remained cautious.
“Market undertone is still fragile with no strong buying commitments. Nonetheless, we noticed there had been some net foreign inflows over the past two days,” he told Bernama.

Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank and CIMB fell two sen each to RM9.90 and RM7.01, respectively. Tenaga Nasional and IHH Healthcare slid four sen each to RM12.54 and RM7.88, respectively, while Public Bank rose one sen to RM4.51.

In active trade, BIG Caring Group and MYDCD gained one sen each to RM1.09 and 59 sen, respectively. CBH Engineering added 2.5 sen to 66 sen, MMAG Holdings went down half a sen to 1.5 sen, while Zetrix AI was flat at 5.5 sen.
