c34b7a42bfdd05df: WASHINGTON: Contracts to purchase previously owned US homes plunged to a record low in October as higher mortgage rates suppressed demand for housing.

The pending home sales index dropped 4.7 per cent to 63.0 last month, the lowest level since the series started in 2001, the National Association of Realtors said on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast that contracts, which become sales after a month or two, would fall 2.0 per cent. October marked the second straight month of large decreases.
Pending home sales declined 16.7 per cent year over year in October. Sales fell during the month in all four regions.

"Two consecutive months of record-low pending contracts point to very sluggish fourth-quarter home sales closings, and annual existing home sales could be the lowest since the mid-1990s," said Lawrence Yun, the NAR's chief economist.
The NAR last week reported a drop in home resales to the lowest level in more than 16 years in October.

Mortgage rates have remained elevated as the US-Israeli war with Iran drags on. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.18 per cent last week, after jumping to near a three-year high of 7.4 per cent in mid-October, data from mortgage finance firm Freddie Mac showed.
bc751934862bca22: WASHINGTON: US single-family homebuilding rebounded in October, but the improvement is likely temporary, with permits for future construction dropping to their lowest level in over 3-1/2 years as high mortgage rates continued to depress housing demand.

The housing market has been in a slump since mid-2024, a downturn exacerbated by the US-Israeli war with Iran, which is fanning inflation and driving up borrowing costs, leaving many young Americans unable to afford to buy a home. Economists expect the housing market downturn to persist in 2027, especially with the Federal Reserve forecast to continue raising interest rates after next month's widely expected hike to quell inflation.
The report from the Commerce Department on Wednesday followed on the heels of a survey this week showing sentiment among single-family homebuilders diving to a more than 14-1/2-year low in November.

"Homebuilding remains in the doldrums, with elevated borrowing costs hurting developers by squeezing demand while significantly raising the cost of construction," said Bradley Saunders, North America economist at Capital Economics.

Single-family housing starts, which account for the bulk of homebuilding, increased 4.0 per cent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 864,000 units last month, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said. Building permits for single-family housing projects tumbled 8.7 per cent to a rate of 772,000 units, the lowest level since January 2023. Building permits fell in all four regions, with a double-digit decline in the West.

The rate on the 30-year fixed mortgage has surged by 120 basis points since the conflict started in late February, data from mortgage finance agency Freddie Mac showed, averaging 7.18 per cent last week. Financial markets have priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike at the US central bank's December 8-9 meeting and anticipated another increase in borrowing costs in January, CME's FedWatch tool showed.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Wednesday the central bank needs to get more aggressive ‌in its response to inflation that he fears is changing public psychology about prices, and either approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.
The Fed left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent range last month.

In addition to elevated mortgage rates suppressing housing demand, homebuilding is also being constrained by the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, which the National Association of Home Builders said on Tuesday was "keeping legal workers off construction sites, deepening labour shortages and driving up costs." Developers were also facing growing cost pressures from high energy and material prices.
An overhang of unsold new homes on the market is also constraining single-family homebuilding.

Residential investment, which includes homebuilding, has contracted in eight of the last 10 quarters. The housing market drag has not dented the economy, as it accounts for a small share of gross domestic product.

Starts for housing projects with five units or more, a very volatile segment, soared 25.5 per cent to a rate of 433,000 units in October. Multifamily housing starts increased 22 per cent on a year-over-year basis. Overall housing starts rebounded 9.9 per cent to a pace of 1.309 million units. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast starts rising to a rate of 1.245 million units.
They rose 2.8 per cent on a year-over-year basis in October.

Building permits for multifamily housing projects fell 5.2 per cent to a rate of 475,000 units last month. Overall building permits tumbled 7.4 per cent to a rate of 1.295 million units. Economists had forecast permits rising to a rate of 1.377 million units.
Permits declined 8.7 per cent on a year-over-year basis in October.
f8e3ad4ed7d214a3: LOS ANGELES: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's biggest religion by the middle of the next decade as the birth rate among Muslims outpaces the number of babies born to women of any other faith, the Pew Research Center projected on Wednesday.

While Christianity has ranked as humanity's largest religion for centuries, the global Muslim population has grown much faster and is forecast to reach 2.57 billion by 2035, compared with a projected tally of 2.52 billion Christians in that year, the Pew study found.

If recent trends hold, Muslims will outnumber Christians 3.6 billion to 3 billion worldwide by 2070, and Islam will also then account for the largest portion of the global population - 37%, up from 26% in 2020, Pew said. Christianity, meanwhile, is expected to hold steady at around 29%, ranking No. 2 in global proportion.

The study attributes the shift mostly to higher fertility rates in the Islamic world, averaging 3.1 children for each Muslim woman, compared with 2.5 children per Christian woman during the period 2020-2025.
In all other religious categories combined, the birth rate in that period averaged 1.6 children per woman, below the minimum rate of 2.1 considered necessary for a generation to replace itself.

While natural population growth - births exceeding deaths - remains the biggest factor in the changing face of Muslim and Christian demographics, religious switching will also play a role, said Pew, a non-partisan, Washington-based think tank.

Based on past trends, according to Pew, both Islam and Christianity will lose more adherents from switching than they gain, but Muslims are expected to lose far fewer - 8 million between 2020 and 2070, compared with 105 million for Christians.

The world's overall population is projected to increase 29% between 2020 and 2070, with Islam and Christianity the only two religious groups forecast to keep pace with or exceed that growth rate, expanding by 80% and 30%, respectively.

Hindus are growing in absolute numbers but are expected to shrink slightly as a share of the world's population (13.6% in 2070), with Jews projected to follow a similar pattern (0.17% in 2070). Buddhists, meanwhile, are forecast to decline in numbers and as a percentage of global population (2.5% in 2070).

All other faiths combined - including Baha'is, Daoists, Jains, Sikhs and followers of various folk religions - are expected to see a modest rise in numbers, while collectively slipping below 2% of all humanity by 2070, according to Pew.

Moreover, people with no religious affiliation, a category that includes those identifying as atheist or agnostic, are expected to decline sharply as a proportion of the global whole, from 24% in 2020 to 17% in 2070, the study found.
The geographic distribution among religions is also shifting dramatically.

By 2070, for instance, Christianity will rank as the largest religion in the US but not its majority faith, and the Democratic Republic of Congo will surpass the US as the country with the greatest concentration of Christians.

The numbers of religiously unaffiliated people will grow in most countries in the coming decades, but those increases will be entirely outweighed by the dwindling population forecast for China, where most of the world's non-believers currently reside.
b9ad2db64f383b68: SEOUL: South Korea's annual college entrance exam was set to be held nationwide on Thursday as authorities make all-out efforts to crack down on cheating involving smart devices and artificial intelligence (AI), Yonhap News Agency reported.
The College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), one of the nation's most important academic events, will be administered at 1,312 test centres across the country from 8.40am to 5.45pm.
A total of 551,864 people have applied for this year's exam, with authorities deploying some 75,000 proctors and around 8,400 additional personnel to catch cheaters at test centres nationwide.

The government has strengthened anti-cheating measures for the CSAT after the top scorer in this year's certified tax accountant exam recently confessed to cheating with the help of AI and digital devices, sparking a public outcry.
As part of the measures, officials will check every pair of glasses worn by test-takers to detect hidden cameras and hand out stickers to cover buttons on clothing to block any miniature cameras.
All electronic devices will be banned from exam rooms, with test-takers permitted to bring in only pencils.

Authorities will also send two disaster alert messages, designed to reach nearly all mobile phones nationwide and sound a loud alarm even when devices are muted, to detect any phones that have not been handed in.
The government seeks to ban those caught cheating from taking the exam again for 10 years and offer a reward of up to 100 million won (US$75,000) to those who report misconduct.

The CSAT is the culmination of years of gruelling studies for many students and is widely seen as a major life event in South Korea, where the university one attends can heavily influence career prospects.
Given the stakes, the government makes every effort to cater to students' needs on exam day.
All aircraft take-offs and landings across the country will be banned from 1.05pm to 1.40pm to minimise noise during the English listening portion of the exam.
Aircraft in flight, excluding those in emergency situations, must remain at an altitude of 3km or higher under the direction of air traffic control authorities.
In Seoul, subway services will be increased by 27 runs to help students get to their test centres on time.
The local stock market, which typically opens at 9am and closes at 3.30pm, will open and close an hour later to ease morning rush-hour traffic.

84df4b34520cbac9: SHENZHEN: Chinese president Xi Jinping will host US leader Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday for a keenly anticipated first trilateral summit likely to centre around major international conflicts.
The three-way meeting comes with Russia's years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, Trump bogged down in his war with Iran, and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia.
The conclave has stoked fears that the three powerful men may seek to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions on Ukraine's fate without consulting Kyiv or Europe.
Xi, Trump and Putin are expected to convene on Thursday afternoon at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, a group of 21 economies around the Pacific rim.
Each side has given different accounts of what they expect to discuss.
Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature.
Its inclusion would be a mild surprise, given that Xi does not view the conflict as China's problem and that Beijing has refused to condemn it.
The Kremlin has said that the agenda had not been finalised, but it would be hard to avoid discussing Ukraine at the meeting, which is set to last "no more than an hour".
Addressing the Apec gathering on Wednesday, Putin said he expected the trilateral summit to be "highly useful".
The Russian leader, largely shunned by Western powers since his 2022 full-scale offensive, declared that the resultant sanctions on his country had "failed".
"At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is... dialogue rather than ultimatums," he said.
Xi did not speak directly about the trilateral meeting during a speech on Wednesday to open the Apec event.
China has said only that the trio will hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations".
Lavish welcome
Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

Trump has said he is also eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin as well as North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though the latter is not present at the conference, and experts say it is unlikely he will come.
In a sign of the importance that China is placing on the trilateral summit, Xi gave Trump an extravagant welcome on Wednesday.

Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, the Chinese leader personally received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air-force flyover.
It was the first time that China's paramount leader had welcomed a foreign dignitary in person since the 1960s, and reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September.
'Serene authority'

"I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations," Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
In contrast, Putin was welcomed at the airport by Cai Qi, China's fifth-ranked leader, in accordance with regular protocol.
Other world leaders at the Apec meeting include Japan's Sanae Takaichi, South Korea's Lee Jae Myung, Canada's Mark Carney and Australia's Anthony Albanese.
Apart from the centrepiece trilateral, the group is also expected to discuss a range of other topics, including trade policy and artificial intelligence.

"Typically, when Chinese leaders host meetings, every detail is nailed down and China's leader is positioned to project an air of serene authority and control," said Ryan Hass at the Brookings Institution.
"Given the other leaders involved though - Trump and Putin - there is only so much choreography that can be done to eliminate unexpected moments," Hass told AFP.

000c7eec3c44d2c9: Saya kira jika kita bercakap mengenai Umno yang berusaha di Negeri Sembilan untuk membetulkan keadaan bodoh yang mereka sendiri ceburi, kita akan menepuk dahi berkali-kali. Perbuatan Umno dan PAS di Negeri Sembilan sudah terlalu ‘ayoyo dan haiya’ untuk dimuhasabah. Apabila pelajar saya bertanya mengenai pusingan U 10 exco Barisan Nasional dan Perikatan Nasional saya memang kesal. Saya memang berdecit dan menggeleng kepala. Umno dan PAS tidak rajin membaca, dan belajar.

Sepuluh exco BN dan PN yang kurang cerdas itu terdiri Adun Linggi, Mohd Faizal Ramli; Zaifulbahri Idrisi (Chembong), Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Siow Kong Choon (Chennah), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu), Mohd Asna Amin (Lenggeng), Mohd Razi Mohd Ali (Sungai Lui), Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh), Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa (Serting) dan Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat).

Memang terdapat perkembangan baharu susulan surat bertarikh 10 Nov 2026 yang mana Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim bersama 10 bekas exco berkenaan telah membuat pusingan U, tetapi soalnya, mereka adalah pimpinan politik yang dipilih rakyat. Mengapa pimpinan sebegini tidak rajin membaca dan belajar?

Kepada pelajar saya itu, saya menjawab begini; “Betapa bodohnya Umno dan PAS yang berusaha untuk menjatuhkan suami Tuanku Aishah Rohani, iaitu Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Bukan sahaja Tuanku Aishah Rohani adalah berketurunan anak gahara, baginda juga adalah anak daripada keturunan agamawan dan bangsawan yang baik-baik dari Terengganu. Ini sahaja memadai menjadi indikasi untuk menimbangkan banyak perkara.”
Umno dan PAS tidak rajin membaca, dan belajar.

Terlalu banyak telah dipertimbangkan mengenai kedudukan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz dari segi adat dan lain-lain; sekarang masanya tiba untuk menimbangkan kedudukan Tuanku Aishah Rohani, isteri Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz.

Kiat boleh faham jika penyokong Umno bebal. Al maklum perasuah pun masih mereka sokong, tetapi ahli PAS tidak sepatutnya bodoh. Oleh sebab yang menderhaka di Negeri Sembilan itu ada dalam kalangan mereka adalah Adun daripada PAS, saya ingin membawa pembaca PAS ke negeri Terengganu. Ini kerana Terengganu adalah negeri solid PAS. Terengganu juga adalah negeri presiden PAS. Justeru, dalam banyak keadaan Terengganu ada tempat istimewa dalam kepala ahli PAS. Ya, kalau mereka rajin membaca dan mahu belajar.

Leluhur Tuanku Aishah Rohani, iaitu Tuanku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan berasal dari Terengganu. Nenda baginda Tuanku Aishah adalah Haji Su Mahmud (juga dikenali sebagai Che Su Mahmud). Haji Su adalah anak kepada menteri besar Terengganu yang pertama, iaitu Ngah Muhammad Yusof yang berasal dan bertapak di Kampung Batu Burok, Kuala Terengganu. Ibu Haji Su adalah Cik Teh Fatimah Ali.

Haji Su Mahmud dipandang terhormat di Terengganu yang mana sebelum kematiannya pada tahun 1940, beliau telah mewakafkan kediamannya untuk menjadi bangunan Sekolah Menengah Agama (Atas) Sultan Zainal Abidin (SMAASZA). Beliau juga adalah bekas pegawai daerah di Kuala Berang ketika pendudukan Jepun.

Anak perempuan Haji Su iaitu Zainun-Mariam binti Haji Su Mahmud, berkahwin dengan kerabat Terengganu, dan merupakan bonda kepada Tuanku Aishah Rohani (Duli Yang Maha Mulia Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan). Ayahanda Tuanku Aishah Rohani adalah Almarhum Tengku Besar Mahmud (Tengku Seri Utama Raja Tengku Besar Mahmud Sultan Zainal Abidin III Terengganu). Dalam erti kata lain, Tuanku Ampuan Negeri Sembilan adalah cucunda kepada Sultan Terengganu iaitu Almarhum Sultan Zainal Abidin III, merangkap cucu kepada menteri besar Terengganu.

Memahami nasab dan leluhur Tuanku Aishah baik dari jalur ayahanda atau bondanya ini sangat penting. Ini kerana baginda merupakan anakanda saudara kepada tiga orang Sultan Terengganu iaitu Almarhum Sultan Haji Muhammad II Muadzam Shah, Almarhum Sultan Sulaiman Badrul Alam Shah, dan Almarhum Sultan Ismail Nasiruddin yang merupakan Yang di-Pertuan Agong keempat. Ini juga menjadikan baginda Tuanku Aishah Rohani bonda saudara kepada Sultan Terengganu iaitu Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin dan juga bonda saudara kepada Raja Perempuan Perlis Tuanku Fauziah Tengku Abdul Rashid yang merupakan cucunda kepada Sultan Sulaiman Badrul Alam Shah.

Keadaan ini juga meletakkan Tuanku Aishah Rohani sebagai sepupu kepada Almarhum Sultanah Asma Sultan Sulaiman Badrul Alam Shah yang merupakan bonda tiri kepada Almarhum Tuanku Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah dan bonda kepada Sultan Kedah, Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah. Sekali gus menjadikan baginda berpangkat bonda saudara kepada Sultan Sallehuddin.

Dalam konteks orang Melayu, dan adatnya, status anak gahara atau anak raja yang lahir daripada pasangan yang kedua-duanya berdarah diraja atau bangsawan sangatlah mustahak dipertimbangkan. Dalam hal melibatkan pewarisan takhta, anak gahara dianggap mempunyai jurai keturunan yang paling tulen. Justeru, mereka akan sentiasa diberikan keutamaan mutlak untuk menaiki takhta atau dilantik sebagai putera mahkota berbanding anak raja yang ibunya daripada orang kebanyakan (atau bukan berdarah raja). Hal ini adalah untuk mengelakkan konflik di mana pelantikan waris yang bukan anak gahara sering ditentang oleh kerabat diraja atau pembesar negeri. Ia juga merupakan petunjuk kepada keabsahan selain menjadi simbol kedaulatan.

Di Negeri Sembilan soal status anak gahara pernah sekali sahaja tidak dipertimbangkan. Kita faham sistem beraja di Negeri Sembilan mengamalkan sistem pemilihan oleh Undang Yang Empat. Ini misalnya terlihat setelah Almarhum Tuanku Munawir (anak gahara) mangkat pada tahun 1967, Undang Yang Empat ketika itu telah sebulat suara memilih Tuanku Ja'afar (bukan anak gahara) untuk menaiki takhta sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan ke-10. Tambahan pula usia anakanda Tuanku Munawir (yakni Tuanku Muhriz yang merupakan anak gahara) masih muda.

Namun demikian saya tetap percaya jurai anak gahara ini penting dalam masyarakat Melayu terutama apabila berlaku perselisihan menentukan siapakah yang lebih absah menjadi raja. Atas sebab itulah maka takhta Yamtuan Besar dikembalikan kepada jurai Tuanku Muhriz. Jurai yang ‘terbonam’ pula meletakkan keadaan menjadi rumit.

Seperti telah ditunjukkan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani mempunyai keterserlahan jurai baginda dengan cara tersendiri. Baginda bukan sahaja melengkapkan suaminya, Tuanku Muhriz, tetapi menjadikan kedudukan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan itu istimewa dengan cara unik. Bukan sahaja kehadiran baginda itu meletakkan Negeri Sembilan bertaut dengan keluarga diraja negeri lain, hari ini bahkan baginda adalah bonda kepada dua daripada empat Putera Berempat Negeri Sembilan. Mereka adalah Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz; dan Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin Tuanku Muhriz. Pemilihan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan mendatang akan dipilih oleh Undang yang sah hari ini daripada Putera Empat.

Makanya, jawapan saya kepada pelajar saya memang valid dan relevan; bahawa ahli Umno dan PAS mesti terus membaca agar pandai. Malulah sudah diundi rakyat tetapi masih bebal. Supaya kita yang sedikit cerdik ini tidak menepuk dahi seraya mendecit ‘ayoyo atau haiya’ melihatkan tingkah laku mereka. Ini kerana dari segi Adat Perpatih, mahupun pertimbangan Adat Temenggung (disokong isterinya), Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir beroleh markah penuh.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
24abcf689c6b9b5d: From Terence Netto
Former Sarawak DAP vice-chairman Wong King Wei has advised DAP to stay out of the Dec 12 Sarawak polls, citing the need for DAP to be friendly with the idea of state autonomy for Sarawakian parties.
Sarawakians want to assert the interests of their state after years of deferring to federal interests.
Decades-old reticence about their interests has in recent years been replaced by an assertiveness that Putrajaya cannot but respect.
The intensive battle between competing political coalitions in the peninsula makes the courtship of Sarawakian (and Sabahan) political parties imperative.
These days, the keys to Putrajaya, for peninsula aspirants, lie between Kuching and Kota Kinabalu.

Since the major Sarawakian parties have banded together into a fairly cohesive force in Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), it does not make sense for DAP to be at cross-purposes with GPS components in the upcoming state polls.
As a single party, DAP may well emerge with the highest or second highest number of parliamentary seats in the next general election (GE16), which is due by February 2028.
No single party or coalition is expected to gain a simple majority in GE16.
This will require one or the other coalition in the peninsula to importune GPS to back them for the right to form the federal government.

DAP, as the anticipated holder of a sizeable number of seats in the peninsula, will be critical to negotiations with GPS, which is expected to sweep not only the state seats in the Dec 12 polls but also the parliamentary ones in GE16.
After seeing how the peninsula Malay vote is solidifying behind Umno and PAS-led Perikatan Nasional, DAP must think strategically about GE16.

Based on their performance in the Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka polls, DAP's Pakatan Harapan (PH) allies PKR and Amanah are struggling to make a dent in the Malay vote, and are no more confident of the non-Malay vote bank.
Fear of the evolving collaboration between Umno and PAS will keep the Chinese vote with DAP despite discomfort with DAP’s overly compliant attitude towards Anwar Ibrahim.

DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook, presently unencumbered by ministerial duties, will have more time to espouse the reforms championed by PH that have been neglected by Anwar's puzzling pussyfooting.
The path is open to a de facto premiership by Loke – by careful rhetoric and subtle gesture – given Anwar's continued tepidity in pursuing the reformasi agenda.
Nuanced rhetoric and statesmanlike gestures by Loke can restrain Sarawak DAP leader Chong Chieng Jen from remonstrating against a DAP decision to refrain from contesting in the Sarawak polls.

DAP should also signal to Rafizi Ramli’s Bersama to be realistic about its chances in GE16, which will require the PKR splinter to go only for the parliamentary seats – 10 at the most – that the Rafizi claque in PKR can win in GE16.
After two underwhelming outings in Johor and Melaka, Bersama ought to come down from the clouds and see that there is no point in overrating its chances.

So, it’s a rearguard action that DAP must undertake, running into GE16, to save what can be salvaged from the growing wreck of Anwar's myopia and Amanah’s failure to convince the Malays that moderate Islam is not a delusion but a viable proposition.
It’s the high road that beckons DAP which also happens to be the pragmatic road to take in the circumstances.
Terence Netto is a senior journalist and an FMT reader.

f84fc13c9a93f718: BENGALURU: Elon Musk said on Wednesday he felt "pretty foolish" about the amount of money he spent on this year's US midterm elections after Republicans suffered sweeping losses.

The CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, and the world's richest man, spent nearly half a billion dollars to back Republican candidates and keep Texas red — a state home to his automaker Tesla, rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.

c17cbd0891fbb3f6: SUVA: Fiji has declared a national state of disaster after an El Nino-driven drought caused widespread water shortages, with the Pacific nation's weather bureau forecasting below-normal rainfall until at least April.

In a national address on Wednesday, prime minister Sitiveni Rabuka said the declaration would allow his government to scale up its response by mobilising resources and coordinating assistance as conditions continue to worsen.
"Families across Fiji are concerned about the availability of water and the effects of prolonged dry conditions on their daily lives," Rabuka said.
"Farmers are worried about their crops and livestock, while communities, particularly in remote and maritime areas, face growing pressure on their water supplies. These concerns are real."

Rabuka said his government has set aside 20 million Fiji dollars (US$8.5 million) for the national response, redeployed from existing funds, to ensure emergency water supplies for families and farmers.
The state of disaster has been declared for one month, with the government able to extend or revoke it based on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council.

El Nino is a natural climate pattern in which surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, causing weather extremes around the world, including drought in some regions and flooding in others. Some scientists say global warming may increase its intensity.

The US Climate Prediction Center said last week that El Nino is strengthening, with a greater than 79% chance of a strong-to-very-strong event through January to March. Australia in June said El Nino could intensify in the second half of 2026 to become one of the strongest in seven decades.
Fiji's national weather bureau warned in October that strong El Nino conditions persist across the tropical Pacific.

Rainfall is likely to remain below normal from November through April, while daytime temperatures are expected to exceed normal levels through January across most of the country, the Fiji Meteorological Service said.

254fb2fb91acd553: The USA’s new ban on Chinese companies remotely accessing GPUs will have short-term impact, but ultimately see China accelerate its development of domestic alternatives, according to Martin Lau, the president of Chinese web giant Tencent.
Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business.

“It does set everyone back. It sets everyone back in China,” Lau said. “So everyone is actually having less advanced compute to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China.”
He said the ban will impact Tencent’s ability to train models.
“Our training efficiency with Hy4 is actually very high,” he said. “When we look at the next version, it would take probably longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run.”
“But over time, the domestic supply chain would actually come on board.”
Lau also thinks the bans won’t hamper Tencent’s ability to run inferencing workloads, because made-in-China chips “should be able to cover it.”

“And over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we see the industry is progressing very fast,” he added. “With the latest restriction, we expect it to actually speed up even further, because all the development effort would actually have to be focused on speeding up the domestic supply chain.”

Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China.

Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem.
But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted.

“In terms of cloud, if it is non-GPU related, we can actually build capacities ourselves outside of China,” he said. “I think there is still a lot of such opportunities because our cloud service is actually very cost competitive. When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore. We may be able to work with some partners in different places.”

Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting.
The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users.
One Tencent biz that went backwards was its international gaming unit, which saw revenue fall nine percent.

Chief strategy officer James Mitchell said that slowdown wasn’t caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. “I think that in fairness, the slowdown for us predated the run-up to GTA VI,” he said, before predicting that Tencent’s existing and future “evergreen games” should help to turn things around.
“The game environment globally is one where the rate of innovation has slowed somewhat, and now with AI, there’s opportunities to re-accelerate innovation,” he said. ®

57de9e1d8f19559c: What began as a political impasse over the absence of a state executive council and the inability to convene the state assembly has descended into further chaos, with a new candidate for menteri besar proposed to the Yang Dipertuan Besar while the incumbent remains in office.

It is understood that during their meeting two days ago, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir allowed Ismail Lasim to continue serving as menteri besar. So why is Umno proposing another candidate for the ruler's consideration? Could Negeri Sembilan end up with two menteris besar?
So, what happens next in Negeri Sembilan?

Ismail and Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi have both expressed their desire to resolve this crisis, regardless of who instigated it, so that the state government can administer sans the unnecessary drama.
Now, I fully support what appears to be the sincerity of these two Malay leaders.
As I understand it, Ismail took the first step towards breaking the deadlock by withdrawing a letter seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz as the state's ruler.
Ismail requested an audience with the ruler – said to be granted for Friday morning – while the 10 state executive councillors withdrew their court action and were ordered to pay legal costs.
The epilogue to this convoluted saga was fast approaching, and the public was prepared to move on to a new chapter.
But, alas, came an unexpected twist in this drama.
Umno announced that Ismail had resigned.
I initially assumed the resignation intended to reset relations between the politicians and the constitutional ruler, starting with the menteri besar's departure.
It sounded like a reasonable move. After all, Ismail and the 10 executive councillors had done plenty to incur the ruler's displeasure, which even I found unforgivable.
So it seemed encouraging that Umno wanted to put the past behind it and start afresh.

However, the Negeri Sembilan palace has yet to verify the Juasseh assemblyman's resignation as menteri besar. The comptroller of the Negeri Sembilan royal household said the supposed letter was sent only by an individual named Hamidi, who claimed to be from a law firm.
Under the state’s constitution, the menteri besar must submit his resignation to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, and it only takes effect with the ruler’s consent.
The palace's desire to verify the letter's authenticity certainly raises questions about it. At that point, Ismail seemed unsure which script he was supposed to follow.

Ismail's son spoke out, questioning the authenticity of the resignation letter and earning a rebuke from Zahid, who asked why family members were wading into the matter when it was an administrative issue.
Zahid has a point, but the letter itself remains perplexing.
And just as the public was trying to make sense of these conflicting scenarios, another unexpected development unfolded.
Tuanku Muhriz summoned Ismail for an audience ahead of schedule. Their meeting lasted an hour and a half.

We thought Ismail, who entered the palace as menteri besar, would emerge as an ordinary assemblyman, as Umno had announced. Instead, he walked out of the palace still holding the post of menteri besar!
So much for the audience with the ruler being the finale to this drama.
But Zahid remains adamant that only one name was submitted to Tuanku Muhriz for approval as the new menteri besar, even though Ismail is still carrying out his duties as instructed by the ruler.

For much of my life, I thought Anwar Ibrahim's imprisonment and black eye were part of the most unforgettable political saga I had ever witnessed. But I must admit, this drama is quite something, too.
What initially appeared to be a confrontation between Umno and the palace has turned into a power struggle within Umno itself.
Why is Zahid determined to replace Ismail, who now has the palace's consent to remain in office?

If Umno's top leadership wants to write another script, perhaps it should put it on hold for a year or two. Give the people of Negeri Sembilan some breathing space. This soap opera with its endless twists and turns has left us winded – though for the people's sake, I hope this saga finds some closure.

fbe1739af67044ec: The app gives short, interactive lessons using quizzes, flashcards, and other easily accessible formats in three languages
Originally published on Global Voices
Screenshot of views of VotEDU on the App Store. Fair use.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

Moldova is a relatively small post-Soviet state with a population of three million people. A landlocked country, it has a long border with war-torn Ukraine and Romania; with the latter, it shares the same official language. The territory that is now Moldova was once part of the Russian Empire, and later the Soviet Union, and Russia has been meddling in its affairs.

Moldova has a large Russian-speaking population and a problematic unrecognized territory: Transnistria, which is basically controlled by Russia. It also has European aspirations and was officially named a candidate to join the European Union in 2022, after Russia invaded neighbouring Ukraine.

The country’s most recent parliamentary elections were held in September 2025, and despite the record influx of Russian disinformation and other meddling, elections were recognized as fair and democratic by the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OCSE) observers. The pro-European Party of Action and Solidarity (PAS) won the elections with a small majority.

The initiative supported by Digital Spark is an app called VotEDU, which answers basic questions about the democratic institution of elections for high school students in Moldova. It does so through short, interactive lessons using quizzes, flashcards, and other easily accessible formats in three languages: Romanian, Russian, and English, and is the subject of this Spotlight story.
Global Voices interviewed the app’s developer, Vlad Garbuz, about the impact of Digital Spark and his initiative.
Global Voices (GV): Please tell us about your organization and why you chose to get involved with the Digital Spark project.

Vlad Garbuz (VG): I started VotEDU, an independent civic-education project in Moldova, to help young people understand democracy before they vote for the first time. The idea began at the VOTech hackathon in Moldova. I joined Digital Spark because I wanted to turn it into a tool that students could use in everyday life and teachers could bring into class. The project helped me build the app and begin testing it with the young people it is meant for.
GV: What issue or challenge in your community prompted you to undertake this project?

VG: Young people meet politics every day through their feeds, long before they enter a polling station. In Moldova, many young people encounter misleading claims online. Yet many have very few easy ways of asking questions about elections and getting the answers they can understand.

That made me wonder how civic education could reach young people in the spaces where they already spend their time. VotEDU was the answer. It puts short lessons, simple explanations, and activities on their phones, so they can learn at their own pace.
GV: What are the key changes or activities that you implemented during your participation in the project?

VG: During Digital Spark, VotEDU developed into a civic-education app with nine units, 28 short lessons, quizzes, interactive activities, and a glossary of 136 civic terms. The content is available in Romanian, Russian, and English. All of the lessons have been reviewed for accuracy and political neutrality. Student privacy guided the app’s design. A short guide was also prepared for teachers.

VotEDU was represented at Moldova Digital Summit 2026, where several educators expressed interest in trying it in schools. The app is now being piloted with high school students in Moldova through its web version. It is also available on the App Store, with the Google Play version coming soon.
GV: How did your participation in the project impact your beneficiaries and the community you serve? Please provide examples.
VG: Teacher feedback has highlighted the need for digital tools alongside Moldova’s electoral education textbook. VotEDU brings these topics into a format students can explore on their phones.

High school students in the pilot program are using the app and sharing feedback. The feedback tells us how easy the information was to access, as well as appreciation of the app’s design, quizzes, and illustrations. Together with teachers’ suggestions, this feedback is helping improve the content in the app and making it a better user experience.
GV: How has your own knowledge, awareness, and experience with digital democracy and civic space changed?

VG: I have learned that the design of a civic tool is part of its message. If an app is hard to understand, available in only one language, or careless with privacy, it may leave out the very people it hopes to reach.

Building VotEDU has made me more careful about how I explain civic topics. Each lesson needs to be accurate and fair, while still being simple enough to use on a phone. I now think more about whether young people feel comfortable asking questions and forming their own views, not just whether the information is online.
GV: What are the most valuable lessons and experiences you are taking away from this project?
VG: The lesson I will carry forward is to start earlier. Young people should have a chance to understand democracy before an election campaign is asking for their attention.

I have also learned that a good idea needs to be tested with the people it is meant to help. Building VotEDU was only one part of the work. Now students are using it and telling us what they think. Their experience will help us see what works, what is still unclear to students, and what needs to change.
GV: What comes next? How will you apply the learning and digital capacity you have built?

VG: I will continue the pilot program and use feedback from students and teachers to improve VotEDU. I plan to bring it to more schools, including rural schools, and use short questions before and after the lessons to see what students learn.

In October 2026, I also demonstrated VotEDU at MEGAPHONE & e-Society in Skopje. I showed how digital tools can make civic education more useful and engaging for young people, and inspire others to try similar ideas. VotEDU is a project that can be adapted for different countries and topics. Making the project public and accessible is one of my objectives to ensure anyone can easily build something that will bring benefits to their local community.
Written by Daria Dergacheva

1fe64ea7de7e2767: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in.

2e6c2de35f87f5db: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — For passengers travelling on board the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)، passing beneath the Titiwangsa Range between Gombak in Selangor and Bentong in Pahang may seem like just another part of the journey. But beneath the mountains is one of the project’s greatest engineering achievements. At 16.39 kilometres long، the twin-bore Genting Tunnel is not only a crucial link in the ECRL network but also showcases the engineering expertise، specialised technology and painstaking work required to carve a path through the rugged terrain of the Titiwangsa Range. Today، the Genting Tunnel holds the distinction of being the longest rail tunnel in both Malaysia and South-east Asia. “It takes approximately 6.2 minutes to traverse the entire tunnel at an average cruising speed of 160 kilometres per hour,” ECRL Head of Infrastructure Design Mohd Rahiman Ab Rahman told Malay Mail during a recent media familiarisation trip. While passengers traverse the tunnel in just over six minutes، its construction presented a far greater challenge، particularly navigating the varying geological conditions beneath the 300-million-year-old Titiwangsa Range. The giant that eats mountains Because the terrain consists predominantly of hard granite، which causes significant wear and tear on heavy machinery، a custom-built، one-of-a-kind open-type hard-rock tunnel boring machine (TBM) was deployed to meet the challenging geological conditions. Built by China Communications Construction Group in Shanghai، the machine measures 266 metres in length، has a boring diameter of 8.98 metres and weighs approximately 1,600 tonnes، tasked with boring through rock formations that have taken millions of years to form. Moving at a maximum rate of 700 metres per month، the TBM excavated the tunnel، transported the excavated material to the surface and installed the concrete lining panels. At the front of this rock-devouring machine، the cutterhead alone weighs approximately 900 tonnes، measures 25 metres in length and has a diameter of 8.98 metres which is the same size as the tunnel diameter. The tunnelling work took approximately two years to complete، culminating in a major breakthrough on July 12,2025. Mohd Rahiman said the Genting Tunnel was unique because it was excavated using a TBM rather than the open-cut method، given the significant overburden pressure exerted by the immense weight of rock and soil above the tunnel alignment. He said passengers may not realise that as their train passes through the single-track tunnel، they are travelling beneath Genting Highlands، with as much as 750 metres of rock and earth separating them from the surface above. To put 750 metres of overburden into perspective، it is equivalent to almost two KL Towers stacked on top of each other underground. “Some of the early challenges involved dealing with water ingress — when external groundwater or surface water breaches the underground structure through rock fractures — as well as rock bursts (caused by the release of stored energy within the rock)، ” he said. Inside the tunnel، Mohd Rahiman said emergency exits are provided at 450-metre intervals to allow passengers and crew to evacuate safely in an emergency، while the tunnel’s design also incorporates a Climate Change Factor (CCF)، with flood protection measures based on a 200-year return period. “The technology used to make the Genting Tunnel possible is truly innovative and a marvel because China is far ahead when it comes to tunnel excavation. “Ultimately، it comes down to combining Chinese technology with adaptations to suit Malaysian conditions، ” he said. While passengers may not pay attention to their journey beneath the Titiwangsa Range، the Genting Tunnel’s significance to the ECRL is anything but hidden.
f69537b793e5e685: SEOUL, Nov 19 — US President Donald Trump repeatedly hinted in the last hours that he may meet Kim Jong Un in China, but Pyongyang has only published photos of its leader visiting a ski resort and the Korean peninsula’s highest peak. AFP looks at whether the odds of a meeting have risen and how a sacred mountain may offer a clue into Pyongyang’s plans. What’s that mountain? Trump, who met the North Korean leader three times during his first term, raised the possibility of another face-to-face as he flew to Asia this week for two sets of regional summits. Beijing said Tuesday it had “no information” on a possible meeting, but hours later in Manila, Trump said Kim “would like to” meet in China. Pyongyang has so far remained mute on Trump’s remarks, instead releasing photos of Kim visiting a ski resort and Mount Paektu, the Korean Peninsula’s highest peak and a sacred mountain for North Koreans. What appears to be a visit to a tourism site may carry more meaning as Kim is known to visit the mountain, where Pyongyang claims his father Kim Jong Il was born, ahead of major decisions. He went to Paektu in late 2013 before the purge and execution of his powerful uncle, Jang Song Thaek. He climbed the mountain again in 2017, weeks before announcing North Korea’s participation in South Korea’s Pyeongchang Winter Olympics, paving the way for a brief thaw in inter-Korean ties. Some analysts say his latest visit could signal another major decision, potentially involving a trip to the Apec summit in Shenzhen. “The mountain is revered as a sacred site in North Korea and holds deep symbolic significance,” Yang Moo-jin, former president of the South’s University of North Korean Studies, told AFP. “Even if talks with the United States do not take place in Shenzhen, I believe he may have used the visit to refine his longer-term strategy toward Washington,” said the expert. Will Kim fly? Known for preferring trains over planes, the mode of transport for Kim to get to the summit in southern China’s Shenzhen may also weigh on his mind. Of the 12 times he has travelled out of the country since taking power in 2011, Kim has flown only three times. Two of these were to China in 2018 aboard his private jet, the Chammae-1, although he hasn’t publicly used the ageing aircraft since — raising questions about its reliability. For his historic first summit with Trump in Singapore in 2018, Kim flew aboard an Air China Boeing 747 provided by Beijing, a move widely seen as an effort to maintain China’s influence over Pyongyang as it pursued direct talks with Washington. Some experts say Beijing could again lend Kim a jet for the Shenzhen summit, seeking to retain influence amid Pyongyang’s potential talks with Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin while they all gather in China. “There are practical reasons to fly, too — travelling from North Korea to Shenzhen would take Kim more than 50 hours,” Ahn Chan-il, a researcher originally from North Korea, told AFP. “And it would make sense for Beijing to get involved this way, after even Trump said Kim’s attendance is up to Xi.” What’s there to discuss? Kim and Trump’s past summits were aimed at reaching a lasting deal curbing Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons programme. But they ended without any concrete agreement. Long-running UN sanctions have done little to divert Pyongyang’s course. Instead, it has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law while repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal as permanent and irreversible. In early November, Kim’s sister Kim Yo Jong also issued a vitriolic statement against Washington, saying there was “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”. Analysts believe that Pyongyang’s closer ties with Beijing and Moscow gives it less incentive to engage Washington, complicating Trump’s efforts after his party’s crushing midterm defeat. At this stage, any meeting would likely be a brief encounter rather than a formal summit, with the leaders “exchanging pleasantries and discussing possible next steps,” said Koh Yu-hwan, a professor emeritus at Dongguk University. What’s in it for Trump? “With his party facing a very divided Congress, Trump wants to cast himself as a peacemaker, and North Korea offers an ideal opportunity,” analyst Yang said. But Trump could also face criticism over “double standards” for taking military action against Iran over its nuclear programme while engaging a nuclear-armed North Korea, Koh told AFP. Secretary of State Marco Rubio however rejected suggestions that a meeting with the US president would give Kim credibility. “It’s serious in the sense that the president has never viewed meeting and talking to someone as a concession,” Rubio said. “He’s often made the case, and I think rightfully so, that how are you going to solve problems with people you have disagreements with if you don’t speak to them, if you’re not willing to engage with them?” He underlined that it remained unclear if there would be a meeting or if any talks would bring a good outcome. But “we’ll never find out if we don’t try, and it may not happen, but he’s prepared to do it,” said Rubio. — AFP
d021e3e01b8ba61d: ACCRA, Nov 19 — From the dusty, bustling markets of Accra to the busy streets of Hong Kong, the ubiquitous red-white-and-blue, chequered stripes of the “Ghana Must Go” bag have crossed borders and generations. An everyday utility used to carry anything from clothes and household goods to food, the bag also carries painful memories of mass expulsion and displacement. “Ghana Must Go is here, come and buy. “It’s good, it’s good,” Agnes Ambomah called out in a rhythmic sales pitch from her roadside stall in the Ghanaian capital. “This red one is very good quality. “This one is original,” she said, lifting one for a customer. At the age of 38, she is too young to remember the events that gave the bag its dark name. But for 70-year-old Bashiru Tahiru, the sight of the bag brings back memories he would rather forget. “It’s a bad luck bag. “I don’t use it,” Tahiru told AFP from his clothing shop in Accra’s sprawling Makola market. Tahiru was among the roughly one million Ghanaians forced to leave Nigeria during a government-ordered expulsion of undocumented migrants in the early 1980s. Working as a port labourer in Lagos, he remembers packing his belongings into one of the striped bags as he prepared to leave. He was afraid to be seen carrying it on the streets as it had already become a marker of migrants that the nation had suddenly turned against. Decades later, the anti-migrant tensions that flared up in South Africa this year – including against Ghanaians in the country – brought those memories back. “It reminds me of the kind of suffer I suffered in Nigeria,” he told AFP in pidgin English. Sporting a black-and-white chequered shirt and a black skullcap, Tahiru recalled leaving Nigeria aboard one of several cargo evacuation ships organised by the Ghanaian government. This time, Ghana and Nigeria were allies, leading a diplomatic charge against Pretoria and organising flights to evacuate their nationals. Tensions against migrants The unrest sparked debates on social media about the symbolism of the bag. Some South Africans said that the Ghana Must Go bag’s origins were a reminder that every nation – Nigeria then, South Africa now – has the right to say “enough was enough”. The iconic bags were not spotted among those returning to Ghana and Nigeria, as some carriers, such as Ethiopian Airlines have “prohibited” checking them in, unless secured in a hardcover container, citing frequent damage to airport conveyor belts. The chequered stripes were seen however being hauled by road as immigrants fled South Africa to Malawi, Zimbabwe and Mozambique. The bag’s history stretches back to Hong Kong in the 1960s during the city’s economic boom. Craftsman Lee Wah, founder of Wah Ngai Canvas, is widely credited for transforming the material, which was sourced from Taiwan and Japan, into durable, waterproof bags. As China gradually opened up in the 1970s, thousands of Hong Kong residents used them to ferry goods when visiting mainland relatives. The bags are still hailed as embodying the city’s resilience, although mass production has moved to mainland China. “The Hong Kong spirit is an indomitable spirit... “It means that no matter how hard life gets, you can still see it through,” Lee’s son, who took over the family business but shies away from the limelight, told AFP. Bags filled with ‘love’ In west Africa, the bag – once associated with humiliation of expulsion and poverty – has over the years become an indispensable staple. “It has become a utility bag,” said University of Ghana historian Kweku Darko Ankrah. “The negative connotation attached to migration is no longer there.” Artists and designers have also grown fond of the material. Ghanaian artist Abdur Rahman Muhammad, 38, paints portraits using the bag’s pattern as a recurring background motif. “In my work, it has come to represent resilience, hope and pursuit of dreams,” he said at his Accra studio. In 2007, luxury fashion house Louis Vuitton released its own spin on the bag, leading to accusations of cultural appropriation and insensitivity to its connection to mass expulsions. But it also showed “how the bag has now transformed from poor status to the middle level, and even to the elite status”, according to Ankrah. The bag is also popular among migrant domestic workers in Hong Kong – one of the finance hub’s largest migrant workforce communities. Every Sunday, their weekly day off, Jenalyn Polinar and her Filipino compatriots gather on Hong Kong’s streets to pack the bags with shoes, clothes, noodles and toiletries to be shipped to their home villages. “This is my way to give them my love,” Polinar, 39, told AFP. Nilda Bendo, 56, has used them to send goodies for two decades. It’s a “very simple bag, but (carries) a lot inside”, she told AFP. “It’s full of stuff,” she said, adding that each time it arrives, her family can’t wait to tear it open. — AFP
e141734a1c6207e6: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — It’s a full-circle moment for Malaysian rap-rock group Pop Shuvit، who are set to reunite with US rock band My Chemical Romance (MCR) as their opening act nearly 19 years after first sharing the stage in KL. The reunion comes as MCR brings The Black Parade 2026 tour to Kuala Lumpur for two shows at the TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil on November 19 and 20، marking the penultimate stop of its Asian leg before wrapping up in Jakarta on November 22. The KL shows are also the only shows in MCR’s Asian leg that have an opening act so far، making the reunion more special for Pop Shuvit. “Of course, after 19 years, it’s a full-circle moment for us,” Moots, the frontman of Pop Shuvit, told Malay Mail. “We were the only act to tour with them in Asia back in 2007 and 2008، and then now we’re the only act providing support on their current Asian tour. “There’s no other artists opening in other (South-east Asian) countries.” Beyond their shared stage history، Pop Shuvit have also developed a musical relationship with MCR guitarist Ray Toro through several collaborations. In 2023، Toro produced and featured on the band’s single Space Between Us، which also featured Butterfingers frontman Emmett on vocals. He previously contributed to Destination Nowhere, a 2019 release by Project E.A.R (East Asian Revolution), a collaborative project involving members of Pop Shuvit، alongside artists from across Asia. With that history carrying into their upcoming reunion، Moots revealed that the band had known about the opportunity to open for MCR since last year. As Pop Shuvit will be performing on both nights، they have also prepared two different sets featuring songs from different eras of the band’s catalogue. “I think it will be a split between two different eras of Pop Shuvit — we have the legacy، old school Pop Shuvit from the 2000s and we also have the Project E.A.R songs that we did in the last 10 years. “Those are some of the songs produced by Ray Toro. He won’t be joining us on stage because he has to get ready for his show but we will be performing the songs that he produced as well,” Moots said. Sharing more on their previous experiences، Moots recalled how touring with MCR in 2007 was a steep learning curve that helped Pop Shuvit mature as artists، while praising the band’s generosity and camaraderie towards them as an opening act. He highlighted how MCR shared their stage، equipment and crew with the group، describing the relationship as a brotherhood that has continued into their upcoming KL shows. “The guys were also really nice people. They were friendly and took care of us. With a lot of international acts، support bands tend to be treated separately — you perform and then you leave. But with MCR، it was different. It felt like a brotherhood. “They showed us respect and allowed us to use their stage and equipment. During the last tour، we didn’t have a lighting technician or many of the resources we needed، but the band let us use their crew and team. “Even for these upcoming shows، they’ve been very forthcoming in supporting us and making sure we have a good performance — that’s something I’ve noticed about MCR compared to other international acts we’ve performed with or opened for. They’re genuinely decent، good human beings، ” he said. Aside from that، Moots also revealed that Pop Shuvit together with Project E.A.R will release a five-track EP titled Awake on November 19 which will also feature Thai hip hop artist Dandee and Emmett of Butterfingers. The EP marks the final batch of songs from their collaborations with Ray Toro، with three of its five tracks produced by the MCR guitarist. These include the lead single، also titled Awake، which features Toro. MCR’s The Black Parade 2026 tour will make its KL stop on November 19 and 20. For both shows، general doors will open at 4.30pm، with early access granted to eligible standing ticket holders and a dedicated entrance available for seated ticket holders، while standard standing admission begins at 4.45pm. Official merchandise، box office، Will Call and assistance counters will operate from 12pm onwards. Meanwhile، Pop Shuvit is expected to take the stage at 7.15pm، followed by MCR at 8.30pm.
20007bd249cf3ed0: From P Sundramoorthy

The Kuala Lumpur police chief's recent directive for policemen to fire when they encounter threats, including situations where they have doubts or feel threatened, raises an important question about the use of firearms by law enforcement in a civil democratic society.
The statement followed a serious incident in Gombak where a police officer suffered severe injuries in a machete attack.

Understandably, the safety and security of policemen must never be compromised. Officers who put their lives at risk to protect society deserve institutional support, protection and the authority to respond effectively to dangerous situations.
However, the broader question is whether a shoot-first approach is consistent with the principles of democratic policing.

Criminologically, policemen operate in unpredictable and potentially dangerous environments. They are expected to protect the public, prevent crime and enforce the law, sometimes while making split-second decisions. Their right to self-defence must be recognised and the government must provide the appropriate training, equipment and support.

Nevertheless, the authority to use firearms carries exceptional responsibility. In democratic societies, the determining factor should not simply be whether an officer feels threatened, but whether the threat is sufficiently immediate and serious to justify lethal force.
Differences in threats
There is an important distinction between a perceived threat, an actual threat and an imminent threat to life.

An officer’s subjective apprehension cannot, by itself, automatically justify discharging a firearm. The nature of the threat, the individual’s conduct, available alternatives and immediate danger to others must be objectively assessed.
International standards, particularly the United Nations Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Firearms by Law Enforcement Officials, emphasise necessity, proportionality and restraint.

Firearms should be used only in exceptional circumstances, particularly where there is an imminent threat of death or serious injury and less extreme measures are insufficient. The preservation of human life must remain paramount.

A policy that encourages officers to shoot whenever they experience uncertainty or apprehension could have unintended consequences. It may increase unnecessary fatalities, undermine public confidence and expose officers and the police institution to legal or disciplinary scrutiny.
Excessive or disproportionate force can weaken police legitimacy, public cooperation and effective crime prevention.
Equipping our police force

This does not mean expecting officers to hesitate when confronted with an immediate and potentially fatal attack. They must instead be equipped to make lawful and proportionate decisions under pressure.

Police services in established democratic societies generally emphasise structured use-of-force frameworks that incorporate de-escalation, conflict management, communication and alternatives to lethal force wherever practicable.
For Malaysia, this discussion should encourage greater transparency concerning police standing orders, firearms policies and procedures governing the discharge of weapons.
Public confidence requires firearm incidents to be documented and investigated without fear or favour, with independent scrutiny where death or serious injury occurs.
Accountability, however, must not become a mechanism for discouraging officers from taking necessary action when their lives or the lives of innocent members of the public are in immediate danger.
Police officers and other law enforcement personnel have a legitimate right and responsibility to protect themselves and the public.

When confronted with an imminent and serious threat, particularly an armed attack capable of causing death or grievous injury, they must have the authority and confidence to act decisively, including using lethal force where it is legally justified and necessary.
They should not be expected to expose themselves or innocent people to avoidable danger because of uncertainty about their authority to defend life.

Continuous training in firearms and the use of lethal force is essential. It must not be treated as a one-off exercise during basic training but be ongoing, regularly assessed and updated to reflect changing criminal threats, operational realities, technological developments and international best practices.

The SOPs governing firearms and lethal force must also be reviewed periodically and updated whenever necessary. They should clearly explain the circumstances in which firearms may be used, officers’ responsibilities, reporting requirements and post-incident procedures.
Ambiguous instructions place officers and the public at risk; clear, practical guidance is indispensable.

Ultimately, protecting police officers and protecting the public are not competing objectives. They are complementary responsibilities of a professional law enforcement service. Officers must not be expected to sacrifice their lives unnecessarily, nor should the public face an unrestricted use of lethal force.
The question is therefore not simply whether police should shoot or not. It is whether the circumstances legally, reasonably and objectively justify lethal force.

In a civil democratic society, officers must be decisive when confronting genuine and imminent threats to life, while restraint, professionalism, continuous training and accountability remain integral to the exercise of their authority.
The legitimacy of policing depends not merely on the ability to use force but on knowing when its use is justified and when it is not.
P Sundramoorthy is a criminologist at the Centre for Policy Research at Universiti Sains Malaysia.

04765589d86f3aff: MIAMI: Gamers around the world got their first taste of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever.
The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time.
The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalised US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs.
"GTA VI" launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time (1100 GMT Wednesday) and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight.
New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. "Wasted already. First one, didn't survive long," he told AFP, laughing.
"This is one of the big things in my life... I've been playing GTA for such a long time," Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP.
Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100.
Analytics firm Omdia estimates "GTA VI" could generate US$3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive.
PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored.
'Taylor Swift of games'

In a review for The Verge titled "GTA VI does something impossible - it lives up to the hype," Andrew Webster wrote that "the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it."
Social media users praised the graphics.
"There's one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human," wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652.
Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University's Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an "outlier" in the entertainment industry.
"This is the Taylor Swift of video games," he said.
"The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services," such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter.
Many fans have taken time off to explore the fictional state of Leonida, which is modeled on Florida.
"I'm going to take four days off," said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning his first session "for a very long time."
Human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32%t increase in leave requests worldwide for Nov 19.
Billed as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, "GTA VI" follows a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in Vice City, a crime-ridden city modelled on Miami.
The game received eight nominations on Tuesday for the Game Awards, the US ceremony honoring the year's best video games, which takes place on Dec 10.
Subversion and controversy
Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the game.
The studio delayed the launch twice after a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online, and it was hit by another round of leaks last summer.
The series has long been accused of glorifying violence and crime. It has also become a pop culture symbol of subversion, known for mocking the flaws of American society.
Players can run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at police.

"It's a series that is famous for being always over the top in terms of its representation of violence and different forms of abuse or harassment, for its representations of gender," said Paolo Ruffino, a lecturer in digital cultures at King's College London.
"I don't expect to see necessarily major controversies unless there is something completely new," he added.
No official release is currently planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.
3a856e3ef81692fb: Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation will release a “critical” security update on Thursday between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC.

While we don’t have many details about the latest vulnerabilities – these haven’t been leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – a Wednesday advisory said the highest-severity bugs in the upcoming release are rated critical.
“The issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups,” the foundation said, urging PHP users to “prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available.”
We do know that one of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560.

In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk.

CVE-2026-115560 “requires a very unlikely combination of configuration and specific PHP application code, which we do not expect to occur in practical use of PHP,” Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, told The Register at the time. “The issue can be mitigated with a configuration setting. So for the moment the PHP Security Team has only published an informational advisory on the PHP website, explaining exactly this situation.”
The earlier informational advisory urged users to “set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.”

These unlikely RCE attacks require an application to set “session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start().”
Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications.

The November security release follows a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon, with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites.

While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26.

Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, as early as October 23, according to Dream researchers.

The Israeli AI cybersecurity startup said the attackers targeted organizations across the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and “likely still” have persistent, remote access to compromised organizations’ networks. ®
